articles.title: Lions Under Fire for Update on Jack Campbell’s Scary Injury
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions are facing pushback for their lack of details on linebacker Jack Campbell after his frightening injury. The post Lions Under Fire for Updat...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are facing some pushback from fans for the lack of details in their announcement on linebacker Jack Campbell's frightening injury.

Campbell was immobilized and taken off the field on a stretcher during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings following a hard hit to the head. The team has not shared many details or given an exact account of what injury he may have suffered, which has led to some frustration and confusion among fans and reporters.

Lions Statement on Jack Campbell Draws More Confusion

The team initially took to social media in the hours after Campbell was taken by ambulance to a hospital, saying he would stay there for monitoring.

"Jack Campbell is resting and will remain in a local hospital tonight, for continued evaluation and monitoring. The team will provide further updates as we have them," the team shared on X.

But the Lions then went close to 20 hours without another update, sharing one on Monday afternoon. The team announced that "preliminary" indications for Campbell were positive, but offering no further details.

"Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital," the team announced in a post on X . "Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time."

The vague language of the post left some reporters confused

"Man. This feels really bleak," noted reporter Nate Geary of WGR 550 .

Other fans wondered why the team couldn't be more concrete in its assessment.

"glad its positive but man, if everything was good I don't understand why they're being so cryptic with this," one shared in a post on X . "No ones asking to see his medical chart but you never see pro athletes getting these type general [expletive] updates on their injuries asking for privacy basically."

Reporter Benjamin Raven of MLive.com added that head coach Dan Campbell spoke to reporters shortly after the statement was issued, but offered nothing beyond what the team had already released.

"Dan Campbell doesn't offer anything more other than emphasizing it's positive 'and the prayers are working, keep them coming,' " Raven shared on X .

Lions Teammates Offer Thoughts for Jack Campbell

Several of Campbell's teammates were visibly emotional while medical crews were working on him on the field. Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson appeared to be in tears, telling reporters after the game that the defense rallied in his honor to pull off the upset.

"I think from that point on, just seeing something like that, him being down for so long, I think from that moment on, it was for 4-6, man," Hutchinson said, via the Detroit News .

Several players also expressed concern for Campbell after the game, saying they were praying for him and his recovery.

articles.title: USF forward's free throw form goes viral for looking like a shot put toss
articles.summary: Fans couldn't believe the free throw form from South Florida forward Kendall Puryear.
articles.body:
Kendall Puryear played her first game for South Florida women's hoops on Monday, with the Bulls blowing out Furman 80-54, and despite a great game from her (12 points, nine boards, four dimes and three steals), all everyone wants to talk about is her free throw form.

The Purdue transfer is a career 57 percent free-throw shooter, so maybe she was trying something different. But as fans noted, her form looks like a shot-put throw from her shoulder, which would make sense -- per her Purdue bio, she's a shot put thrower who was ranked No. 1 in Missouri, where she's from.

She missed both of her free throws on Monday and went very viral for her form.

There might be more to this story as the season goes on -- maybe she's trying something new, perhaps she's in the middle of working on her mechanics... we'll see if there's improvement from the 6-foot-3 forward.

articles.title: 3 Best MLB Free Agent Fits For Randy Arozarena If He Leaves Mariners
articles.summary: Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for Seattle Mariners star outfielder Randy Arozarena.
articles.body: Randy Arozarena is a stud. The Seattle Mariners' left fielder and three-time All-Star is in the prime of his career. The soon-to-be 32-year-old is a potent threat from the right side of the plate, a reputable danger on the basepath and a commendable left fielder. He's one of MLB's most well-rounded outfielders and a money hitter in the postseason. Translation: Arozarena is getting the bag, and can be a difference-maker for a contending club or one aspiring to pose such a threat. Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for Arozarena, should the outfielder leave Seattle: Chicago White Sox Regardless of how their 2026 season ended — blowing a 2-0 lead to the Cleveland Guardians in the AL Division Series — the Chicago White Sox are an ascending club, and Arozarena would fit their timeline. Arozarena is coming off arguably the best year of his MLB career, as he led the American League with 113 runs scored and posted a career-high 5.7 wins above replacement and a 148 OPS+ across a full season in 2026. As for the potential fit, the White Sox have a burgeoning positional core, but the bulk of that nucleus comes in their infield, in the form of Miguel Vargas, Munetaka Murakami, Chase Meidroth and Colson Montgomery. Arozarena would likely take over in left field, with the reliable, contact-hitting Sam Antonacci either moving to right field or into a utility role (Antonacci played second base, third base and shortstop in the minor leagues, as well), or Chicago could have the veteran slot into right. Granted, Arozarena hasn't played right field for an extended period of time since 2022. Chicago could hit the long ball last season. In fact, it was fifth in the sport with 211 home runs. At the same time, the White Sox recorded the fifth-most strikeouts (1,494) and were 25th in MLB hits (1,282). Chicago's lineup is a power-heavy unit, and the White Sox have some starting pitchers to be bullish on (e.g., Sean Burke and Davis Martin). Now, they need veteran complements, which is precisely what Arozarena — who boasts a career .292/.380/.565 postseason slash line and blasted an absurd 10 home runs across 20 postseason games for the Tampa Bay Rays in 2020 — would be. With all that said, Chicago may prefer to keep Antonacci in left field and/or spend money on a center or right fielder, rather than signing the best outfielder on the open market and forcing the issue defensively. Toronto Blue Jays Yes, the Toronto Blue Jays probably need another front-line starting pitcher, but their offense also needs a lift, and Arozarena is arguably the most proven hitter on the open market. Arozarena, who has a level power stroke from the right side and traditionally draws a healthy number of walks, would provide a jolt to a Toronto offense that was unrecognizable in 2026. How much did the Blue Jays struggle with the bats last season? They were last in MLB in runs (648) and home runs (152), 26th in slugging percentage (.381) and tied for 25th in on-base percentage (.310). What's more, Toronto was last in average exit velocity (87.5 mph) and hard-hit percentage (34.0%) and 29th in barrel percentage (5.8%), according to Statcast. For context, the Blue Jays led MLB in hits (1,461) and on-base percentage (.333) and were fourth in runs (798) in 2025. So, yes, an impact bat — or two or three — would help here. On the defensive front, Toronto shuffled several left fielders last season, most of them having the versatility to play both corner outfield positions, or in Davis Schneider's case, second base, too. At the same time, Toronto may prefer to back up the truck for an ace-caliber pitcher (e.g., Tarik Skubal), bank on getting more offensive production from its outfield surplus and make moves around the edges on its positional depth chart, rather than put the full-court press on Arozarena. Cleveland Guardians Preaching that the Cleveland Guardians need an offensive lift is a yearly tradition. Be that as it may, Arozarena would be a terrific fit in Believeland. Over the last six seasons, Arozarena has averaged 22.7 home runs, 76.0 RBIs, 25.2 stolen bases, 3.6 wins above replacement and a 124 OPS+ per season, while boasting a combined .255/.349/.438 slash line. As for Cleveland, which took the Tampa Bay Rays to six games in the American League Championship Series, its offense was 27th in MLB in home runs (162) and slugging percentage (.380) and 24th in runs (678) and hits (1,291). Meanwhile, it was 28th in hard-hit percentage (35.0%), tied for 28th in barrel percentage (5.8%) and tied for 25th in average exit velocity (88.1%), per Statcast. Arozarena would presumably start in left field for the Guardians, moving three-time Gold Glover Steven Kwan to center field — where he played roughly half the time in 2026 — on a full-time basis and keep the emerging Chase DeLauter in right field, with midseason acquisition Jo Adell serving as the team's designated hitter/fourth outfielder. Ángel Martínez and/or Petey Halpin would be the first outfielders off the bench. Sure, Cleveland could possibly view Arozarena as a minor upgrade over the potential upside of a generally young outfield core. That being said, where else can the Guardians improve? This is a franchise that prides itself on having elite pitching from top to bottom and has the bulk, if not all, of its starting rotation spots taken up for next season. Patrick Bailey will likely be behind the plate, with Travis Bazzana and Brayan Rocchio in the middle infield spots and José Ramírez at third base. First base is open, but the Guardians could also keep the well-rounded Nathaniel Lowe on a short-term deal. Again, this was factually one of MLB's worst offenses. The Guardians need a boost, and Arozarena is the best bat on the open market, a proven commodity and his arrival would involve minimal defensive tweaks. articles.title: Demond Williams Jr. Expected To Be Washington's Starting QB Vs. Penn State
articles.summary: Demond Williams Jr.’s time away from being Washington’s starting quarterback did not last long.
articles.body: Demond Williams Jr.’s time away from being Washington’s starting quarterback did not last long. Washington head coach Jedd Fisch said Monday that, barring any lingering injury issues, the junior out of Chandler, Arizona, would start the Huskies’ home game against Penn State on Saturday. The move follows Washington’s 17-10 win at Nebraska this past weekend when Williams came off the bench in the fourth quarter and led the Huskies — who had managed just three points in the first three quarters — to an improbable comeback victory. Williams finished 7 for 13 passing for 99 yards. No play was bigger than a 24-yard completion to Chris Lawson on a fourth-and-18 play with 1:42 remaining. That set up a 25-yard touchdown pass to Lawson on a catch-and-run two plays later. "If Demond is feeling good, I don’t see why he wouldn’t play and start," Fisch said. "… He took some hits in that game, so we’ve got to make sure that he’s good to go and that he feels right. If he feels right, hopefully we can play off the momentum of the fourth quarter." Williams had been out since halftime of Washington’s 41-24 loss to Iowa on Oct. 9, when he suffered a fractured rib on the Huskies’ final drive of a first half. He had thrown for 69 yards and was sacked four times. Transfer Elijah Brown replaced Williams and threw for 251 yards and three touchdowns, and then went 21 for 27 for 302 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions in the Huskies’ 38-26 win at Purdue on Oct. 16 while Williams continued to recover. When he was injured, Williams had a 145.7 quarterback rating to begin the year, which ranked 10th in the Big Ten. Brown ended up getting his second straight start, but the UW offense struggled against Nebraska’s defense. Brown went 19 for 30 for 136 yards in the first quarters. Fisch put Williams in to provide a spark, and that’s just what happened. Now, the Huskies will see if he can continue to do so. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 9 lineups
articles.summary: Fred Zinkie offers start/sit lineup advice for some of the top RB2s in fantasy football going into Week 9.
articles.body:
Let's take a look at RB2s in backfield splits, who are listed in the order that they should be started in Week 9. Current roster rates on Yahoo are listed in parentheses.

Note: Braelon Allen has graduated from this list, as his success in the absence of Breece Hall could cause him to remain the starter when Hall returns to action.

Week 8 couldn't have worked out much better for Coleman. The Broncos trailed the Chiefs for most of the game, which caused Sean Payton to take the drastic step of benching starter J.K. Dobbins by halftime. Dobbins logged just one snap and zero touches in the second half, while Coleman took over the backfield in a comeback victory that moved the Broncos ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West standings. Coleman rewarded his coach for the additional opportunities by logging a 51-yard reception and a five-yard touchdown run on the team's final drive of the game.

Although the Broncos' official depth chart lists Coleman behind Dobbins and injured RB RJ Harvey, it's clear that this is Coleman's backfield now. He's easily an RB2 option for a Week 9 matchup against a Panthers defense that has allowed the second-most fantasy points per game to opposing running backs . The one caveat for putting in an aggressive offer for Coleman on the Yahoo Trade Market is the rumor that the Broncos will attempt to acquire Colts RB Jonathan Taylor by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

At first glance, things were status quo in the Rams backfield during Week 8, with Kyren Williams receiving 16 carries in comparison to 11 for Corum. But a closer look reveals that with seven minutes left in the game and the Rams leading 24-9, Williams had logged just five carries. He was used to run out the clock in a lopsided victory over the winless Chargers, while Corum carried the ball more when the game was in doubt.

Maintaining a roughly even split in the Rams backfield is working well, as Williams has averaged 4.9 yards per carry and Corum has produced a 5.2 mark. While it was surprising to see Corum receiving a heavier workload for most of the Week 8 win, it would be premature to dismiss Williams as the team's lead runner. Both players should be ranked among the top-20 RB options for a favorable Week 9 matchup against a Commanders defense that has been average against the run, but has allowed the seventh-most points per game.

Although the critics were lining up for Ashton Jeanty throughout the days leading up to the Week 8 game against the Jets, it was still shocking to see Washington receive 25 carries in comparison to just two rushes for Jeanty. As per usual, Jeanty was heavily involved in the passing game (3-64), while Washington was not targeted.

Washington was stopped four times at the goal line, which contributed to an average of 3.3 yards per carry. Still, the Raiders won for the first time in over a month, and their offense produced 38 points. Perhaps this was similar to the Cam Skattebo situation, where the coaching staff was trying to get the attention of the lead back by dramatically cutting his workload. Or perhaps the Raiders will leave things status quo after a big win and give Washington most of the carries against the 49ers in Week 9.

Washington's upside is somewhat limited by a tough matchup against a San Francisco defense that ranks fifth in rushing yards allowed per game and his lack of involvement in the passing game. But the potential volume on the ground will keep him ranked around RB25, which makes him a borderline RB2.

Monangai missed a fourth straight game with toe and thumb injuries in Week 8, which has surprised fantasy managers and the Bears. After all, Chicago almost certainly would have put Monangai on injured reserve weeks ago if it expected him to miss four games. Given that the hard-charging runner has missed more time than expected, we can assume that he may finally return to action this week.

Monangai may be the Bears' best pure runner. He perfectly combines a physical running style with the potential for long runs. D'Andre Swift has done his best to handle a heavy workload in Monangai's absence, averaging 3.2 yards on 74 carries over the past four games. With the team coming off a short week, head coach Ben Johnson will surely be open to reducing Swift's workload, which would make Monangai an appealing flex option against the Bucs this week, if he returns. Although the Bucs are excellent against the run, a Bears offense that ranks second in rushing yards per game will give them their toughest test thus far. Make sure to monitor Monangai's status in practice this week closely.

Allgeier may have been the best story of Week 8. Injuries suffered in the first half by Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) left Allgeier as the team's only healthy option in a game where they were consistently trailing the Cowboys. The former Falcon put the team on his back down the stretch, scoring on a 63-yard run and a five-yard reception, where he made an impressive stretch to reach the goal line. After Allgeier sparked the offense, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson made big plays of their own and finished off one of the most improbable OT wins of the season.

The Cardinals could place Love on IR, as he has dealt with multiple right ankle injuries, dating back to August. Knight may also be absent in Week 9 while he recovers from his concussion. The coaching staff already prefers Allgeier in passing situations and may give him most of the rushing work as well. Unfortunately, the Cardinals are double-digit underdogs for their road game in Seattle. Arizona will have one of the lowest projected point totals, which limits Allgeier to being a flex option.

The following players will rank outside the top 25 running backs in Week 9 but can be expected to tally 5-10 points for those who are desperate.

The Texans could get David Montgomery (groin) back for Week 9, which would relegate Marks to a backup role that carries notable volume. Marks could convert 5-8 carries and a couple catches into a decent fantasy performance, as the Texans will face the winless Chargers, who are below average in rushing yards and points allowed per game.

The Vikings continue to deploy Jones and Jordan Mason in an even split. In Week 8, Mason logged three more carries than Jones, while Jones caught two more passes than Mason. Minnesota's next game will take place on Monday Night Football against the high-scoring Bills. Jones should get 7-10 touches in that game, and his role in the passing game makes him slightly more valuable in PPR formats.

Some managers may have forgotten that Black gained 53 yards and scored a touchdown on 12 carries in Week 7 before the 49ers enjoyed their Week 8 bye. The team returns to action for a favorable home matchup against the Raiders. Most prediction models have the team as double-digit favorites with an expected point total around 30. If those predictions are realized, Black will likely get 8-10 touches.

The Seahawks' official website listed Zach Charbonnet as the starter as soon as he was activated from IR. But it was Price who led the RB room in touches in a Monday Night Football loss to the Bears, tallying 10 carries and two receptions. The rookie and his teammates did little with their opportunities, as the Bears defense, led by recent acquisition Jeffery Simmons, turned the clock back to 1985 and dominated the line of scrimmage. Price and the entire offense should be more successful in a Week 9 home game in which Seattle is a double-digit favorite over Arizona.

Over the past two weeks, Tampa Bay has turned the clock back 50 years by tallying 105 rushes and 14 passes, with Gainwell reviving his season by rushing for 228 yards on 39 carries. Starter Bucky Irving has been outstanding as well, and the Bucs will likely try to assert themselves on the ground in Week 9, when they travel to Chicago to face the Bears. Chicago has been excellent against the run but will be coming off a short week and could be more vulnerable than usual to a physical attack.

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 9 but are either a trade or an injury away from having significant value.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire, Week 9: Mike Washington Jr. among slew of good RB pickups to consider
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his waiver wire column, providing top pickups for fantasy football in Week 9.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

Lamar Jackson (thumb, potentially season-ending)

Tyler Huntley (toe, potentially headed to IR)

Willis was the featured quarterback in this space last week, even though I highlighted him more as a long-term option than a one-week streamer. That's because of a difficult matchup with the Patriots in Week 8, but Willis once again displayed his high floor with 15.6 fantasy points in the contest. It was good enough to make him the QB16 on the week.

In his previous two outings, Willis finished as the QB4 in Week 7 and the QB13 in Week 5. His outlook is also becoming brighter thanks to the emergence of Miami's young skill position players like Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington, Chris Bell and Ollie Gordon II. Between his rushing upside, the improving talent around him and the schedule boost, Willis will be a streaming option every week and offers an intriguing ceiling against more generous opponents.

Kirk Cousins is 56% rostered but would be the No. 3 QB add behind Willis and Sam Darnold, if available.

Michael Penix Jr. vs. CIN (20% rostered)

Desperation streaming options (if starting)

The Raiders' backfield was one of the more stunning developments in Week 8, with Jeanty playing a season-low 40% of the snaps and only seeing five touches. Meanwhile, Washington played 60% of the time and led the way with 25 carries for 83 yards.

Jeanty still managed 73 scrimmage yards thanks to a 45-yard catch, but this is a terrible shift for his fantasy projections moving forward. After the game, Klint Kubiak suggested this was not a one-game punishment and instead a sign of things to come with their running back room.

Washington has been the top pickup in this column before, as Jeanty entered the season banged up and has looked efficient with his carries all season. The rookie is bringing more juice on the ground and Kubiak clearly wants to see if he can provide a spark there.

You won't find Washington on the waiver wire in any of my leagues, but if he's available in yours it's time to spend up and acquire him. It's possible this evolution continues with Washington earning the majority of the early-down carries and Jeanty making the bigger impact as a pass-cacher. That moves Jeanty down into the low-end RB2/high-end RB3 range and Washington not far behind.

Don't get too excited about Johnson's 128 receiving yards and a touchdown on five catches in Week 8. After all, he only played 19% of the snaps.

The real shock is that he's still available in over 80% of leagues. The fifth-round rookie has been a must-add in all formats for a while, as the high-upside backup behind Kenneth Walker III. The only difference after this week, is that Johnson might begin to provide some flex potential even with Walker healthy.

As we approach the midway point in the season, the recommended FAB bids will increase, especially when it's a player who's one injury away from stardom. Don't be timid when trying to add Johnson this week, he's one of the best stashes to have on your bench.

The Colts look like a team ready for the season to be over, which isn't a great sign after… (checks notes)... Week 8.

The trade rumors surrounding Jonathan Taylor have only intensified since I mentioned McGowan as a stash in last week's column. Taylor even seemed a little emotional on the sidelines in the loss to the Jaguars, perhaps recognizing that it might be his last time in a Colts' uniform.

We still have a week before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10, but at this point I would be surprised if Taylor isn't on a new team by then. As long as Indy doesn't get a starting-caliber back as part of the return for JT, McGowan would be next man up to start — with DJ Giddens as the new change-of-pace option.

For as bad as the Colts offense has been lately, they still have one of the 10 best fantasy RB schedules in the second half of the season, so McGowan could be a sneaky fantasy RB3 down the stretch.

What is going on with the Buccaneers offense? After throwing just 11 times for 64 yards and a touchdown in Week 7, Baker Mayfield somehow topped that feat by only throwing three times on Sunday and failing to complete a single pass.

And yet, the Bucs won both games thanks to incredible efforts from their defense and rushing attack. Bucky Irving is posting some of the best stats of his career, while his backup Gainwell has been nearly as productive with 14 carries for 88 yards last week and 25 attempts for 140 yards in this game.

Despite limited touches early in the season, this is a nice reminder that Gainwell can be dangerous when called upon. We aren't going to see Tampa's recent commitment to the run continue to this degree, but it makes sense for their offense to lean on the ground game. The Bucs are another backfield with a top-10 fantasy schedule the rest of the way.

So, consider Gainwell a fantasy RB3 with a much higher ceiling if Irving were ever to miss time.

Black is a rookie backup I've been featuring in this column all season, encouraging managers to stash him away in case of a Christian McCaffrey injury.

The veteran did get banged up in their last game in Week 7 before the bye, but was fortunately able to return to the game in the second half. That led to increased usage for Black, who rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a score. It was his highest output since a 15-touch, 70-yard stat line in the opener.

McCaffrey downplayed the injury after the game and with the time off, I'd expect him back this week. CMC later confirmed he is dealing with a "mild" hamstring strain. However, it's clear Black is up to the challenge if his number is ever called.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last season isn't the worst idea in the world. Black should be rostered everywhere and would provide RB2 fantasy production with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline. There's also the possibility that the recent string of injuries in the Cardinals' backfield (Jeremiyah Love, Bam Knight) leads to Conner being activated and put into the lineup.

Tyler Allgeier is 52% rostered but would be the No. 1 RB add, if available.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at BAL (26% rostered)

Brian Robinson Jr. vs. CIN (25% rostered)

Antonio Williams/Treylon Burks, Commanders

There isn't a breakout league-winning receiver on the waiver wire this week. Instead, it's filled with a variety of WR3/flex options. That's why you don't need to go wild with your offers and I certainly wouldn't use my No. 1 waiver priority on a wideout this time around.

With Terry McLaurin done for the season, Williams was a hot waiver-wire recommendation last week. Though he didn't blow the doors off with a big stat line, he posted his second consecutive game with over 50 receiving yards in the win over the Eagles. It was also the second straight outing where he led the receivers in snaps and routes run.

His teammate Burks is also intriguing as a flex play. He stepped up before the bye with four catches for 66 yards and came through again in this contest with three grabs for 81 yards. Burks has at least eight fantasy points in four of his last five appearances.

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7 when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 15 fantasy points in his other three outings over the last month, finishing as a top-10 WR each time. Touchdowns helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in those games as well (65, 86, 76).

With A.J. Brown's uncertain injury timeline and Romeo Doubs still on IR, Douglas is stepping up for Drake Maye. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting him as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Mitchell is the most difficult player to write about this week, given my undying hope that his talent will eventually turn him into a strong dynasty asset. Sadly, he was on the bench in most of my dynasty leagues during his seven-catch, 142-yard, one-touchdown eruption against the Raiders.

There's no denying Mitchell has the ability to produce in an NFL offense, the problem remains consistency. It's going to be incredibly tough to trust him in a Jets offense that has so many hands calling for the ball, including Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper Jr., Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Braelon Allen and Breece Hall (when healthy and if he's not traded).

This week it was Cooper who was left with zero in the box score. The week before it was Wilson held to two receptions and 26 yards. That doesn't mean you can't add Mitchell and see how this plays out, but I wouldn't get my hopes up for him turning into a startable asset in redraft. He's more of a boom-or-bust one-week replacement in good matchups.

Jordyn Tyson is 51% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Makai Lemon is 58% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Tyson, if available.

Keenan Allen is 51% rostered but would be the No. 4 WR add behind Tyson, Lemon and Williams, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 53% rostered but would be the No. 5 WR add behind Tyson, Lemon, Williams and Allen, if available.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Gesicki has scored a touchdown in six of his seven outings this season and currently sits as the TE5 in fantasy points per game on the week.

The concerns over his reduced targets the last couple weeks went away with a four-catch, 76-yard, one-score effort against the Titans on Sunday. He's now tied his career-high with six touchdowns and he's accomplished it in just seven games.

At this point, Gesicki has definitely done enough to warrant being rostered in most formats, but remains available in over 80% of leagues.

Even if you don't need a tight end start, Gesicki is in consideration as a flex option. Remember, he's mostly used as a third receiver out of the slot anyway. The Falcons are a plus matchup for both positions, so Gesicki has a good chance to keep this streak going in a potential shootout in Spain.

Quarterbacks: Justin Herbert, Jacoby Brissett, Aaron Rodgers

Running Backs: J.K. Dobbins, Jacory Croskey-Merrit, Emanuel Wilson

Wide Receivers: Chris Godwin Jr., Xavier Worthy, Romeo Doubs

Tight Ends: Mark Andrews, Juwan Johnson, Jake Ferguson

Jacoby Brissett has struggled this season and was eventually benched in Sunday's game. Whether he's replaced for the rest of season by Gardner Minshew or eventually Carson Beck, Brissett's time as the Cardinals starter is nearing its end. His only hope for a fantasy revival would come via trade.

Regardless of what the depth chart says in Denver, J.K. Dobbins has been overtaken by Jonah Coleman. The veteran has played less than 25% of the snaps in each of past two games and there are also rumors the Broncos could be in the mix to trade for a big-name running back like Jonathan Taylor. Even with RJ Harvey on IR, Dobbins can be dropped.

Godwin hasn't topped 50 yards this season and now the Buccaneers have decided to stop throwing the ball entirely. With Emeka Egbuka likely returning soon, Godwin can be safely sent to the waiver wire.

articles.title: Countdown to the Startling Line
articles.summary: This year's special highlights a marathon milestone: 2026 marks the 50th Anniversary of the 5-borough race. Watch Saturday on Channel 7 and wherever you stre...
articles.body:
Join us on Saturday, October 31st for a half-hour special, "Countdown to the Starting Line," hosted by Eyewitness News Anchors Liz Cho and David Novarro.

Liz and David have pre-race highlights and a preview of the excitement leading up to the NYC event...where thousands of runners from all over the world converge on the Big Apple. It's been called "New York's biggest block party."

articles.body:
And since this is your Nebraska/Illinois odds article, let me break down some other odds for you.

In Week Six of the 2026 college football season, Nebraska hosted the Indiana Hoosiers, losing 20-17. But the Huskers' peak win probability was 88.2%. A week later, drawing the latest kickoff time in the country at Oregon, again, leading in the fourth quarter, the Bugeaters' peak win probability was 85.4% before Dylan Raiola came off the bench to lead the Ducks to the 17-14 come-from-behind win.

After the bye week, Nebraska's offense sputtered against the Washington Huskies. But the Huskers still led 7-3 in the fourth frame before eventually collapsing like a dying star into the black hole that was Memorial Stadium, losing 17-10 on the Blackout Night.

These outcomes are more than just bad luck. They are game management breakdowns, play execution failures, and unbelievable results that make Husker fans shake our heads and throw a little kindling under HCMR's seat.

But they are also statistical anomalies.

The likelihood of Nebraska losing three straight games in the fourth quarter despite leading the rest of the game (the opening minutes of the Indiana game not-withstanding) are 1-in-4,920, or about 0.0203%.

Folks, we're breaking into "best 3-9 team in college football history" territory. We opened the season with five straight wins and have played well enough to win two of the last three. I don't think we played well enough to beat Washington. I'll rephrase…the offense and special teams didn't play well enough to beat the Huskies. It's difficult to ask the defense to do more.

So now it's time for a Friday night game in Champaign, taking on Bret Bielema's Fighting Illini. Illinois did to Oregon what Nebraska was either unable or unwilling to do…rush the passer and win the game. Then on Halloween, Illinois beat a rudderless, interim-coached Maryland squad 20-17. The Illini are also 5-3 but have a 3-2 record in Big Ten play.

It's a Friday night game and the Huskers are going to have to once again rely on their defense. Illinois is averaging 29.0 points per game. Their conference losses were to a Julien Sayin-led Ohio State and Purdue. Again, the 2026 Big Ten is pure chaos.

The FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Illini as a 4.5-point underdog to the visiting Huskers. That makes sense since the Husker players are "pissed off" following the Washington game. Meanwhile, the over/under is currently at 49.5.

articles.title: Murray, Wentz or trade? The pros and cons of Vikings QB options
articles.summary: With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Minnesota faces a difficult decision — and they can't afford to get it wrong again.
articles.body:
The Vikings are 6-1, have one of the NFL's most talented offensive rosters and somehow find themselves staring at another quarterback dilemma with the trade deadline just one week away.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell says K yler Murray remains Minnesota's starting quarterback , provided his sore hamstring doesn't keep him out of Monday night's showdown with the Buffalo Bills. But a report Monday suggested the Vikings haven't ruled out anything , including a trade for another quarterback.

Names like Daniel Jones, Kirk Cousins, Justin Herbert and even Gardner Minshew have been floated by insiders, former players and fans, with some suggestions carrying considerably more weight than others.

So what should the Vikings do? They have four options, none of which comes without risk.

Pros : Murray has shown flashes of being the right guy, and if he can find a way to play at a consistently high level, the Vikings could have a functioning, perhaps even dangerous, offense. He's more mobile than any alternative option, not to mention the Vikings don't have to give up draft capital or create another public QB controversy if they shift to Wentz.

Cons : Murray and Minnesota's offense are the main reason Minnesota's undefeated start to the season ended in Detroit. There hasn't been enough growth in five full Murray starts to move forward with confidence, and the schedule is daunting, with games against the Bills, Packers and 49ers in the next three weeks. Sticking with Murray could result in the Vikings being 6-4 and at the bottom of the stacked NFC North by the time we get to Thanksgiving.

Pros : Wentz has played seven games since signing with Minnesota last year, and while his performances have been up and down, he's been able to move the ball through the air at a more efficient rate than Murray. He's also gotten Justin Jefferson involved, and that's a priority right now after Jefferson uncharacteristically let his frustration boil over on the sideline in Detroit.

Cons : He's a statue. How many sacks will he take that Murray can avoid? And while Wentz might be better equipped to get the ball to Jefferson, is he really good enough to take Minnesota on a deep playoff run?

It also puts O'Connell and the Vikings in another uncomfortable situation after letting Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones leave after the 2024 season, and then not signing Aaron Rodgers when it was apparent that he wanted to be in Minnesota. Then they traded J.J. McCarthy, who might be turning into a star in New York. Benching Murray would be another QB disaster, but it might be inevitable either way.

Pros : This is where Kirk Cousins fits into the discussion. A reunion would be thrilling, and the fact that he's second in the NFL with 19 touchdown passes and third in the league in passing yards while taking only 11 sacks in eight starts (Murray's been sacked 15 times in five starts) is intriguing. He falls into the "small QB trade" category because the cost to get him wouldn't be anywhere near the price to acquire someone like Justin Herbert. Cousins would give the Vikings' offense a jolt, and the learning curve would be minimal because he's familiar with O'Connell's offense.

Cons : Cousins is 38 and immobile, so the risk of him getting mauled behind a leaky Vikings offensive line is real. His contract is also a bit of a pain. If they acquire him, they'd owe him $10 million guaranteed in 2027, so even if they cut him to avoid the two-year, $80 million club option from taking effect on the fifth day of the 2027 league year, they'd still have to eat $10 million in dead money.

Pros : Daniel Jones and Justin Herbert play in this category. Herbert would be tantalizing, even though he's been horrible this season for the winless Chargers. He's the big-arm, pocket passer who could thrive in O'Connell's system. He's under contract through 2029, meaning the Vikings would have their long-term answer.

Of course, this assumes the Chargers would even entertain trading Herbert. They're 0-7, but he's still a franchise-caliber quarterback under contract through 2029. Los Angeles might be more interested in rebuilding around him than starting over without him.

Jones knows O'Connell's offense, and his return, even though it's after his 2025 Achilles injury, might be ideal because the Vikings reportedly wanted to keep him after Darnold left in the spring of 2025. Jones is the cheaper option, but he's not signed beyond 2027.

Cons : Trading for Herbert would probably cost the Vikings multiple first-round picks. His contract is large enough that it would make it more difficult to sign players who'll need new contracts in the offseason, including core defensive starters Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Isaiah Rodgers and Jalen Redmond.

Jones, meanwhile, just might not be very good. His track record is ugly outside of the first eight games last season, when he had 13 touchdown passes and three interceptions as the Colts got off to a 7-1 start. He had five touchdowns and five interceptions in the next five games before tearing his Achilles, and the Colts lost four of those five games.

The Vikings have spent nearly two years trying to find the right quarterback for O'Connell's offense. They've moved on from Darnold, Jones and McCarthy, passed on Rodgers and now have a 6-1 team that might need another quarterback change to keep its Super Bowl hopes alive.

At some point, the Vikings have to get this right. And with the trade deadline one week away, they're running out of time.

articles.title: Spurs' Castle bounces back from migraine-plagued game
articles.summary: The third-year guard was his old self in Monday's win over Utah after he went scoreless against Minnesota on Saturday.
articles.body:
Stephon Castle bounced back from a scoreless outing plagued by a migraine to put together 16 points, five rebounds and four assists in the Spurs' 119-97 win over Utah on Monday night at the Frost Bank Center.

The third-year guard had five rebounds, four assists and a steal in Saturday's 121-111 home victory over Minnesota but missed all four of his shots from the field in 22 minutes while suffering through his first scoreless game since Dec. 29, 2024 of his rookie season and only the third goose egg of his career.

In 26 minutes Monday, Castle was 7 of 16 from the field, including 2 of 7 from 3-point range. He also recorded a block.

Castle called the migraine a "random kind of thing." He didn't get the green light to play from the medical staff until after going through warm-ups.

"I've had a couple in the past, but it wasn't too bad," he said. "In the morning, it was kind of bad, but as I came into the game, it got better."

Castle's fellow guards picked up the slack offensively against the Timberwolves, with Dylan Harper finishing with a career-high 25 points and De'Aaron Fox providing 22.

"We have so many weapons and so many things we know teams can't guard," Castle said. "Whether one guy's having a bad night or a couple guys aren't shooting the ball well, I feel like we have so many wrinkles and so many guys that can just make a play out of nothing."

articles.title: Michael Brandsegg-Nygard Is Punishing the NHL and Scoring Too
articles.summary: Michael Brandsegg-Nygard is among the NHL's hardest hitters, and the only one in that group producing. #RedWings
articles.body:
Michael Brandsegg-Nygard continues to be a factor in Detroit. Not only does he contribute on the score sheet, where he is tied for third among NHL rookies in points with Vegas's Trevor Connelly, but he contributes on the defensive and physical side of the game as well. Brandsegg-Nygard, known to Red Wings fans as MBN, has 70 hits in 15 games played , and he is a positive difference-maker for this year's Detroit Red Wings and a breath of fresh air for a fan base that is fed up.

Michael Brandsegg-Nygard Is a Coach's Dream

MBN is a coach's dream. The kid makes plays, scores goals and lays the body down. His physical presence makes space on the ice and complements his shot and passing ability in a way that benefits the team, and the best part is that he is still a developing rookie. Not only is he tied for third in rookie points, he is also tied with Minnesota's Yakov Trenin for third in hits in the entire NHL. He has been near the front of this rookie class since October, when he paced every NHL rookie in assists .

A Goal, an Assist and Seven Hits in Florida

Brandsegg-Nygard contributed to Monday night's 5-3 win over the Florida Panthers, scoring 45 seconds after assisting on Justin Faulk's power-play goal that gave the Red Wings the lead in the third period. He finished the game with a goal, an assist and a plus-1 rating . Offensive contributions, check. Defensive contributions can be checked off too: besides the positive rating, MBN had seven hits , the most on his team and tied for the game high with Florida's Brady Tkachuk. For some comparison, both Tkachuk and MBN had seven hits, but Tkachuk finished with an assist and a minus-1 rating .

The Only Top-10 Hitter With Double-Digit Points

After Monday's win, Michael Brandsegg-Nygard sits at 70 hits and 10 points in 15 games played. He is the only player in the NHL's top 10 in hits who has reached double figures in points. Kiefer Sherwood, the league leader at 85 hits, is next in that group at nine points, and nobody else in it has more than eight.

Needless to say, we as fans are loving how he is playing the game, and he is no doubt worth getting excited over. Personally, if he maintains this level of play, he has a great shot at winning the Calder Trophy, and at the very least he will be in the conversation.

articles.title: Manny Diaz on FSU rumors: 'I'm really, really happy here'
articles.summary: Duke head coach Manny Diaz responded to chatter of him possibly being a candidate for the Florida State job on Monday.
articles.body:
After back-to-back nine-win seasons, an ACC title and with Duke standing 6-2 this year, it's inevitable that bigger programs will be looking at Manny Diaz as their possible next head coach.

On Monday, Diaz answered questions about that, especially regarding Florida State , where Mike Norvell was just fired after six-plus seasons.

"Last year, my bags were packed for Penn State. I addressed the team last night. I made it pretty clear I'm really, really happy here. I love being here." Diaz said. "Internet rumors are going to be internet rumors. I told the coaches and players the same."

It makes sense that the Seminoles would consider Diaz a possible replacement. The 52-year-old coach was born in Miami, coached the Hurricanes and has deep ties to the Sunshine State, which puts out as many quality players as any other state. Diaz has also taken Duke to new heights with a limited budget, something that wouldn't be a problem in Tallahassee.

Still, while getting to a bowl game and winning nine games a season will make you a hero in Durham, the pressure would rise to the nth level if he took over a Florida State program where championships are expected.

Diaz is also aware that his players might be facing the same decision.

"I told coaches and players we're the same," he said. "Everybody thinks our players are going to go somewhere else. So it's a cause of success, which I'd rather have than the alternative."

articles.title: Ipsum Sports will continue as the Official Training Center of the Academy
articles.summary: Girona FC and Ipsum Sports have renewed their collaboration agreement for one more season, thus consolidating an alliance aimed at the development and perfor...
articles.body:
Girona FC and Ipsum Sports have renewed their collaboration agreement for one more season, thus consolidating an alliance aimed at the development and performance improvement of the Club's youth academy players.

Under this agreement, Ipsum Sports will continue as the Official Training Center of the Girona FC Academy, providing its expertise, methodology, and facilities to the footballers in Girona FC's youth categories.

The collaboration allows Academy players to complement the work they usually do with the Club's various teams through specific sessions at Ipsum Sports Girona's facilities. The work focuses on areas such as strength, injury prevention, readaptation, recovery, and neuromuscular assessment, always in coordination with Girona FC professionals.

This continuity reinforces the Club's commitment to providing its youth structure footballers with the best possible tools for their development. Ipsum Sports' methodology, based on individualized work, scientific knowledge, and the application of technology in training, allows players to complement their daily routines and adapt the work to the specific needs of each footballer.

Girona FC president Delfí Geli positively valued the renewal of the agreement: "The training of our players goes far beyond football work. We want the Academy footballers to have the best tools and professionals to continue growing, and the continuity of the collaboration with Ipsum Sports allows us to keep strengthening this crucial area of their development."

For his part, Edu Garcia, founder of Ipsum Sports, highlighted: "Renewing this agreement is a sign of mutual trust and commitment to the training of young footballers. At Ipsum Sports, we want to contribute to preparing them to face the physical demands of football and accompany them through the different stages of their careers."

Ipsum Sports is a center specialized in physical preparation, injury prevention, and sports readaptation, with extensive experience in footballers. It integrates scientific knowledge and technology to design individual programs for performance improvement and recovery until the return to training and competition.

articles.title: Most common players on eliminated teams from Week 8 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues — plus FAB waiver wire advice
articles.summary: Death Leagues have claimed more star players. Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski advises you on how to approach the waiver wire in Week 9.
articles.body:
Every week I'll examine the most common NFL players on the teams eliminated in Yahoo Death Leagues, trying to figure out where the puck is headed. I will also offer some FAB advice ($1,000 cap is the Yahoo default), but please remember this area is highly context-sensitive and manager-specific.

For the first six weeks, I used this space to talk up the long game. I like to trust myself (and my depth) in the early weeks, and take heart that it's not that difficult to beat just one team when the league is still large.

The rules are starting to shift now. Eight of your opponents are checked out for the year. Keep in mind the bye weeks are here — the Steelers and Titans don't play in Week 9. Injuries also continue to mount , part of why these games are so challenging, and downright cruel at times.

In the first month of Death League season, I'm going to trust the size of the league and be confident I can beat just one of the teams. As such, I'm not proactive on early offers. I'm definitely more proactive now, but remember that the strength of each cut team becomes much stronger as we get deep into the season. Be very careful not to to cripple your remaining budget for the future.

I'll still offer bidding in three buckets, and you'll need to season the recommendations to taste. You know your context and league habits better than an outsider would. But just know the immediacy has stepped up a bit. I still think it's a mistake to spend all of your money in the present — the wire gets stronger and stronger in every passing week — but I also understand the gravity at hand. So don't be afraid to get in there with some competitive offers.

My weekly FAB recommendations will come in three buckets:

Proactive : This means you highly covet this player, perhaps might even need this player. I realize these offers might not win if someone in your league is lighting money on fire, but as described above, that's often a short-sighted mistake in this format.

Reactive : This means you desire the player but the offer has to make sense for your short- or long-term strategy.

Keep Them Honest : This is an offer that is not designed to win, but might surprisingly land a player if your opponents are distracted by other talent available or unexpectedly passive that week. I often compare notes with other experienced Death League players and we're surprised at how often the Keep Them Honest offers actually win (this is also a portable strategy for regular season-long leagues; you never know when strange market behavior will come about).

One last note : Understand that the FAB recommendations are with the assumption that you won't be making offers for every available player.

Week 8's top-10 players on eliminated teams

He's been unstoppable most of the year, but the latest Lamar Jackson injury sunk him in Buffalo. Tyler Huntley also might miss multiple weeks, which means the Ravens offense could be under water. But Flowers is such a talent, we have to keep the light on for him.

Taylor's value is likely to rebound for one of two reasons; either he'll be dealt to a contender, or he'll stay with the Colts and thrive on a favorable second-half schedule. But the next week or so could be bumpy as everything sorts out.

A busted thumb has Jackson on IR and it's possible he's done for the year. Baltimore's season could be on life support, too.

Between Tampa raindrops and a nightmare day for Michael Penix Jr. (four interceptions), the Atlanta passing game never got off the ground in Week 8. The Bengals present a good rebound spot this week, but then it's a mess: Chiefs, bye week, Vikings. London's rep remains the same; he's a very good player, but just short of a superstar.

His touchdown slump has reached four games, and he's failed to make double-digit fantasy points in two of three starts. It's hard to fault Robinson much when he's still averaging 5.2 YPC, but the Falcons need to find more ways to get him involved as a receiver.

8. RB Christian McCaffrey, 49ers (16.1%)

Hard to fault a guy on his bye week. McCaffrey's efficiency is no longer dreamy, but he's a bell cow on a scoring offense, so cut the big check.

Perhaps hamstring and shoulder injuries kept Pickens down in the shocking loss to Arizona. Owner Jerry Jones is calling for Pickens to get more work forward, an interesting spin on the "squeaky wheel" narrative. The Cowboys still have a narrow target tree, so Pickens makes sense as a proactive get.

Given how injured the Niners are at receiver, the Week 8 bye wasn't unwelcome. If Mike Evans can stay on the field, Purdy can still be an elite fantasy option. But if Evans has any hiccups, all bets are off.

articles.body: Connor McDavid and Sidney Crosby are two of the most recognisable captains in the National Hockey League. But their reported homes reflect noticeably different lifestyles. McDavid’s reported home is all about entertaining and modern functionality.Connor McDavid’s Edmonton mansion reflects modern luxuryConnor McDavid’s reported Edmonton mansion stands out for its contemporary architecture and carefully planned living spaces. articles.title: Caitlin Clark's childhood bedroom secret inspires new book EXTRAordinary as WNBA star reveals emotional family connection
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has revealed the special childhood item that inspired her first children’s book, EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark has revealed the special childhood item that inspired her first children’s book, EXTRAordinary! A Little EXTRA to Reach BIG Dreams. The Indiana Fever star told PEOPLE that a mirror in her childhood bedroom in West Des Moines, Iowa, played a big part in shaping the book. Clark says the mirror still holds a special place in her life, and she hopes to pass it down to one of her children someday.Caitlin Clark’s childhood bedroom mirror inspired her new book EXTRAordinary!Clark’s parents, Brent and Anne, had the mirror made for her before she was born, and it has remained in the same bedroom ever since. Even after she moved away to attend the University of Iowa, her parents kept it in their home. Whenever Clark visits them, she still spends time in her old room and looks at the mirror that has been part of her life since childhood.Speaking to PEOPLE, Clark explained why the item means so much to her and how it became the inspiration for her debut children’s book, released on November 3.“It’s a super personal thing for me. My parents still have it up there. They still live in the same house, so a lot of it speaks to my story and the way I was raised.”The mirror has a hand-painted message at the top that reads, “The difference between ordinary and extraordinary is the little EXTRA.” Its sides are decorated with several short messages, including “Know Love,” “Celebrate,” “Cherish Family,” “Eat Chocolate,” “Believe and Pray,” “Smile,” “Learn Lots,” “Watch Sunsets,” “Set Goals,” “Spa Day” and “Show Courage.”These words were more than just decorations for Clark. They were daily reminders of the things she should value while growing up. She also has a funny connection to one particular message, as her parents seemed to know about her love for sweets long before it became clear.“It was a mirror I looked in every single day, and it’s just always been a great reminder,” Clark said.Talking about the message encouraging her to eat chocolate, she added that her parents’ prediction about her sweet tooth had turned out to be true.“I have the biggest sweet tooth in the world, so maybe the mirror played into that a little bit.”For Clark, the mirror reflects the lessons her parents wanted her to carry through life. She also hopes to keep it in the family for years to come.Caitlin Clark shares family traditions behind EXTRAordinary! and her love for readingThe basketball star told PEOPLE that she wants to hold on to the mirror for the rest of her life and possibly give it to her children when they are older.“Maybe pass along to one of my kids one day,” Clark said.Her new book also shares parts of her journey in basketball and the values she learned at home. Clark believes that small efforts and the support of loved ones can make a big difference when someone is working toward a dream.Her interest in books also started at home. Clark’s mother, Anne, studied English in college and always encouraged her children to read. The family even had a Christmas Eve tradition in which Clark and her brothers received a book chosen by their parents.Each book came with a personal note written by their mother. Clark still goes back to read those messages, especially when she wants to look back at her childhood and the people who helped her through difficult times.She now hopes to carry that tradition forward when gifting her own book to friends this Christmas. articles.title: Texas, Star Madison Booker Still Chasing A National Title After Transfer Exodus
articles.summary: Madison Booker and Texas made it to the Final Four twice in a row after 20 years away, but a new season brings a new roster with new challenges.
articles.body: Madison Booker and Texas earned a No. 1 seed in the NCAA Tournament for the third consecutive year, and made it to the Final Four twice in a row after 20 years away. Then the Longhorns watched three key players walk out the door. That's life in the modern era of the transfer portal and player mobility. The exodus has hardly seemed to phase Longhorns coach Vic Shaefer and the team they left behind, or tempered the expectations surrounding the program. With do-everything All-American Booker still leading the way, Texas starts the season ranked No. 6 and is considered a strong threat to No. 1 South Carolina for the Southeastern Conference championship. Texas opens the season Wednesday night against Fairleigh Dickinson. Still, it was a surprise when the Longhorns returned home from a Final Four loss to UCLA and watched Jordan Lee transfer to South Carolina, guard Aaliyah Crump transfer to Duke and forward Justice Carlton transfer to Houston. "That broke my heart, but at the end of they day, they are individual players and have to do what’s best for them," Texas point guard Bryanna Preston said. All three played big roles in chasing Texas' first national championship since its only one in 1986. Lee and Crump were two of the biggest transfer moves in the country. Lee was Texas' No. 2 scoring leader at 13.2 points last season and is a top-level perimeter defender. She started and scored 13 in her South Carolina debut against Maryland. Crump was limited because of injuries last season but was one of the top recruits in the country out of high school. Booker seemed little interested in looking back or even wondering why a former teammate would leave. "I mean, that's their journey," Booker said. "What they thought is going to be better for their journey is what they thought. I'm supporting them always." Preston Replaces Longtime Leader Harmon Over the past five seasons, Texas leaned on point guard Rori Harmon on both ends of the court. Harmon is the only player in Division I history with more than 1,500 points, 900 assists, 600 rebounds and 350 steals. She is now in the WNBA with the Washington Mystics. Harmon was tiny but she dogged opponents with relentless defense and was typically assigned to defend the opponents' top perimeter player. That is likely Preston's job now. "Rori was fast. Bri’s electric. I’m excited to see her this year. She’s really special. I don’t worry about her running our team or doing things for us on offense," Schaefer said. "What we’ll have a hard time replacing is the defense. Who is going to step to be that No. 1 defender?" Booker Brings All-American Experience To Championship Chase Booker drives Texas. As a freshman, she took over Harmon's point guard duties when Harmon was sidelined for most of the season with a knee injury. With her size, ballhandling and free-flowing jump shot, she is a matchup nightmare for smaller guards and slower forwards. She's also no longer a kid. She's a fourth-year player who has already taken her place in program history and now wants to bring home a championship. Booker also comes into this season off the worst game of her career in the Final Four loss to UCLA. Booker shot just 3 of 23 with a string of 17 consecutive misses. Her driving layup to get Texas within one in the final 20 seconds was blocked. It was her second bad game in a Final Four. Booker scored only 11 points in a blowout loss to South Carolina in 2025. "It's a new year and a new team. That loss was heartbreaking ... but it's in the past, we move on. That was my mentality," Booker said. Booker needs just 31 points to become the program's fourth career 2,000-point scorer. After the loss to UCLA, Booker took a month off and then returned to practice with a clear motivation to chase the elusive national championship. "I thought about what I need to get better and that was to be a three-level scorer ... and use my voice to put confidence in a young group," Booker said. "That's my whole approach. I can't be good without my teammates." Schaefer and the Longhorns will be leaning on her again. "In my mind, Madison Booker is the best player in the country," Schaefer said. "Every night when we take the floor, I feel good about that." Reporting by The Associated Press. articles.title: Canada's Prime Minister Says Russia Not Allowed at World Juniors After 6 Countries Threaten Boycott
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Russia will not be allowed to play at the upcoming world junior hockey tournament, adding to a growing boycott led by European federations ahead of the men's tournament next year in Germany.
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that Russia will not be allowed to play at the upcoming world junior hockey tournament, adding to a growing boycott led by European federations ahead of the men's tournament next year in Germany.

Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia and Denmark came out with statements signing up for a boycott of games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. A top sponsor of the world championships next year threatened to walk away, after Finland announced Monday it was rallying other nations to refuse to play Russia.

Carney said Canada respects those decisions but that the nation had its own call to make. The world juniors, featuring the top men's players under age 20, is being held in the province of Alberta beginning in late December.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal and unjustified horrific war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," Carney said. "So if you're asking specifically about the world juniors, the Russians will not be there."

In a statement released minutes after Carney's comments, Hockey Canada said it "thanks the government of Canada for today's strong position that Canada intends to prevent Russian and Belarusian officials and athletes from participating under their national symbols in international sporting events taking place on Canadian soil.

Hockey Canada's board of directors is meeting this week. The International Ice Hockey Federation and USA Hockey are also having meetings to discuss what has become one of the hottest topics in the sport since the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled last week that the IIHF must reinstate Russian teams, beginning with the world juniors

Russia and Belarus have been excluded since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Canada's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Anita Anand, Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship and Secretary of State for Sports Adam van Koeverden said in a letter that the government would use existing federal law to prevent national teams from Russia and Belarus from competing under their national symbols.

"This measure is not directed at the Russian and Belarusian people," they wrote. "Rather, it is intended to prevent the governments of Russia and Belarus from using international sporting events hosted in Canada as platforms for state representation, political legitimacy and propaganda."

Austria told The Associated Press it is weighing whether to join the six others in boycotting, and Germany is unsure of hosting the men's championship.

There was no immediate reaction from the IIHF to the boycotts. USA Hockey did not respond to a message seeking comment.

Hockey power Sweden adds weight to boycott movement

The Swedish hockey federation said its board decided Tuesday that it would not play against Russia but would still play other games. That was a turnaround from last week, after Sweden initially indicated a boycott was off the table following the CAS ruling Friday.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," federation head Anders Larsson said in a statement, using the team's nickname.

The Swedish statement came shortly after Norway announced its boycott.

"Our position is that Russia should be excluded from all international championships as long as the war in Ukraine continues and remains unchanged," the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said in a statement. "At the same time, this decision is based on our responsibility to protect the safety and wellbeing of our players, team staff and their families. We believe that playing Russia under the current circumstances could expose our players and team staff to significant security risks. Our priority is therefore their mental health, wellbeing and personal safety."

Norway referred only to the men's world championship in May in its statement. General secretary Petter Salsten told the AP that, in the case of the world juniors, Norway would potentially be removed from the tournament by the IIHF to make way for Russia. In that case, "if RUS is added, it is a huge possibility that NOR is out," he wrote via email, because Norway was the last team to qualify.

The chairman of Denmark's hockey federation told the Ritzau news agency its teams would not play against Russia. Latvia's federation said it "reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

The Austrian federation told the AP in an emailed statement: "We stand behind the decision of Finland and Norway and are currently looking into whether the European nations will join a boycott together. We are therefore not ruling out a boycott and are still coordinating with the authorities on this."

Finland is the defending men's world champion and Norway was the bronze-medal winner this year.

The growing boycott is similar to the situation in soccer in 2022, shortly after the Russian invasion of Ukraine. On that occasion, all of Russia's potential World Cup qualifying opponents threatened to boycott. FIFA successfully argued at CAS for excluding Russia on the grounds that not doing so risked "irreparable and chaotic" harm to the competition.

Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian Tyres said it will no longer sponsor the world championship if Russia takes part.

Tiina Frazer, senior vice president for brand, marketing and communications, said that "under the current circumstances, continuing the sponsorship if Russia participates would not be aligned with our values."

Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, a tournament sponsor since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown if Russia plays.

Previously, the chief executive of Germany's hockey federation said it could pull out of hosting the men's world championship over concerns about costs and security.

Junior tournaments are affected, too, with the Finnish city of Turku saying it will not co-host next year's world juniors if Russia participates.

The Czech federation is hosting the women's under-18 world championship in January and said Tuesday it would speak with the government about whether Russian players would be denied entry to the country.

One political figure in support of Russia's return is Slovakia's pro-Russia Prime Minister Robert Fico.

"I've also always wondered what the value of a gold medal is, if on the way to it you don't have to beat the Russian hockey players, who are undoubtedly among the best in the world," he posted on social media Saturday.

The women's world championship starting in Denmark this week is not affected by the CAS ruling and is going ahead without Russia.

Associated Press writer Karel Janicek in Prague contributed to this report.

articles.title: 3 Best MLB Free Agent Fits For Michael King If He Leaves Padres
articles.summary: Here are the three best MLB free agent fits for star right-hander Michael King if he leaves the San Diego Padres.
articles.body: Want an ace, but don't want to spend the $300-400 million it may cost to sign Tarik Skubal? Meet Michael King. The San Diego Padres' star right-hander recently opted out of the final two seasons of a three-year deal, putting an All-Star-caliber, top-of-the-rotation starting pitcher on the open market. Since becoming a full-time starter for the San Diego Padres in 2024, King has been one of the best right-handers and starting pitchers altogether in the sport. Here are the three best free agent fits for the 31-year-old King should he depart San Diego: Athletics Enough is enough: The Athletics need to make a sizable investment in their starting rotation. One season after sporting a collective 4.70 ERA, the A's starting rotation surrendered the most home runs in MLB (150) in 2026, while being 29th in ERA (5.61), WHIP (1.50) and opponent batting average (.272) and giving up the fourth-most walks in the sport (338). The lone bright spot was J.T. Ginn, who posted a 3.71 ERA and 3.4 wins above replacement over 138 ⅓ innings pitched (24 starts, 27 appearances). To recap: A lot of help is needed on this front. Two seasons after posting a 2.95 ERA and posting 201 strikeouts in 2024, King recorded a 3.21 ERA, a 127 ERA+ and 4.3 wins above replacement over 185 innings pitched in 32 starts in 2026. King pitches deep into games, evades damage and would give the A's a much-needed rotation anchor in his prime. Plus, veteran Jeffrey Springs, who has made 59 starts for the A's since 2025, is a free agent. While their bats collectively underwhelmed last season, the Athletics still have a compelling positional core highlighted by Tyler Soderstrom, Nick Kurtz, Shea Langeliers and Jacob Wilson, among others. In 2025, they were fifth in the sport in hits, seventh in home runs and slugging percentage and eighth in OPS. Yes, the A's won just 64 games. At the same time, the Houston Astros won the American League West at 81-81 and were swept by the Chicago White Sox in the Wild Card Series. With mere middle-of-the-pack starting pitching, the A's can make a run at the division, and signing King would be a major step in that direction. So, why aren't the A's the No. 1 fit for King? For starters, he fits any team that needs an ace. The other reason is there are just teams closer to contending than them. Houston Astros The pixie dust is running low on the Astros' mystique; King would breathe needed fire into their club. After an impressive regular season, King was spectacular for the Padres in the playoffs, surrendering just one run over 14 innings pitched, which included coming out of the bullpen to get the final six outs of the team's Game 3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Division Series, which extended San Diego's season another day. King, who consistently throws four pitches (sinker, changeup, four-seamer and sweeper) while mixing in a slider, has been money in the postseason, with the right-hander boasting a career 1.86 ERA and an 0.76 WHIP over 29 combined innings pitched. He'd be a lifesaver for an Astros' starting rotation that surrendered the most walks in the sport last season (378), while being 27th in ERA (4.81) and WHIP (1.40). Now, Houston does have 2025 All-Star Hunter Brown (3.19 ERA in 20 starts in 2026), and Peter Lambert is coming off a respectable season (3.82 ERA in 29 starts). At the same time, Tatsuya Imai struggled in his first MLB season (4.93 ERA and a 1.42 WHIP in 15 starts and 23 appearances), with Mike Burrows doing the same in his first season with the Astros (5.99 ERA and a 1.55 WHIP in 17 starts, 18 appearances). Meanwhile, Cristian Javier continues to be held back by elbow and shoulder injuries, with elbow issues also limiting Hayden Wesneski. Either way, the Astros — whose offense led MLB with 226 home runs in 2026 — need another healthy starter, with a starter of King's ilk boosting their chances of contending in an AL that had just two teams win 90-plus games last season (the AL-champion Tampa Bay Rays won 98 games, and the New York Yankees won 93 games). All that said, there's a team that needs King slightly more, and it's the club that sent the Astros home in the AL Wild Card Series. Chicago White Sox The White Sox are on the rise, but they need veteran enhancements across the board, and that starts at the top of their rotation. King would be the undisputed ace and most proven starting pitcher in Chicago's starting rotation, providing a needed lift to a unit that was 26th in ERA (4.60) and tied for 24th in WHIP (1.34). Moreover, their starting staff was last in innings pitched in the regular season (674 ⅔) and manager Will Venable only got 17 ⅔ innings from starting pitchers/openers across the team's seven postseason games. How is that last note even possible? On the bright side, right-hander Sean Burke (3.34 ERA and 4.2 wins above replacement across 27 starts and 32 appearances in 2026) looks like a future All-Star and left-hander Davis Martin (3.95 ERA in 28 starts, 29 appearances) has shown promise. Add King to their rotation, and the White Sox have their veteran leader. Chicago has a power-heavy offense (the White Sox, who have a budding offensive core that includes infielders Miguel Vargas, Munteka Murakami and Chase Meidroth, were fifth in both runs scored and home runs last season), while the aforementioned Burke and Martin look like long-term rotation shoo-ins. Now, Chicago needs to get the proven commodities to complement both units. The White Sox had the Cleveland Guardians on the ropes in the AL Division Series, winning the first two games of the series in Cleveland before losing three consecutive games and the series altogether. Better starting pitching likely would've punched the White Sox a ticket to the AL Championship Series (Cleveland scored nine runs in both Game 3 and 4). Adding King would arguably make Chicago the best team in the AL Central. articles.title: Rajkumari Chanu scripts history with maiden Wushu bronze at Youth Olympics Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian wushu celebrated a landmark moment at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games as Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu clinched a historic bronze medal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian wushu celebrated a landmark moment at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games as Rajkumari Lanchenbi Chanu clinched a historic bronze medal in the women's Changquan combined event, becoming the first Indian to win a Wushu medal at the prestigious multi-sport competition.Chanu secured the third position in the final with an aggregate score of 18.039 points, putting together impressive performances in both disciplines. She scored 8.723 points in Gunshu before adding 9.316 points in Changquan to seal her place on the podium.The medal is a significant breakthrough for Indian wushu, a sport in which the country has been striving to establish a stronger presence on the international stage. Chanu's achievement has not only brought recognition to her individual efforts but also offered a major boost to the sport's growing ambitions in India.Her podium finish also took India's medal tally at the ongoing Games to three. The young wushu exponent followed the medal-winning performances of Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada, who claimed silver in the women's 63kg judo category, and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu, who secured bronze in the women's 100m freestyle. Both had delivered their performances on Monday.Chanu's success is expected to provide fresh impetus to the development of wushu among India's younger sporting generation. Her performance underlines the potential of emerging Indian athletes to compete against the best at the international level.The historic podium finish is also a reward for the efforts of her coaches, support personnel and the wider wushu fraternity, who have contributed to her development.For Indian sport, Chanu's bronze represents more than another addition to the medal count.
