articles.title: Sam Burgess: Warrington Wolves head coach signs new two-year deal
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess signs a new two-year deal.
articles.body:
Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess has signed a new two-year deal.

The 37-year-old former dual-code England international has won 63 of his 99 games since being appointed for the 2024 campaign.

During his time in charge they have twice finished runners up in the Challenge Cup final and were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in last season's Grand Final.

He confirmed after last month's Old Trafford defeat that he had "given his word" to owner Simon Moran to stay on for next season.

"It's a real honour to extend my time at the Wire, and I'm excited to continue leading this club forwards," he told the club website. , external

"I love what we're doing and believe we're not far away from achieving what we are all chasing."

Warrington finished third in Burgess' first season in charge before slumping to eighth in 2025.

However, with the experienced Steve McNamara brought in as assistant, they bounced back well last season to finish third again and reach a first Grand Final since 2018.

McNamara has since left to take over at Hull FC.

"Sam is a vital part of what this club is building. His trust and passion for youth development have allowed some of our most talented pathway products to thrive in a first-grade environment," director of rugby Gary Chambers added.

"To reach three major finals in three years shows how close we are to achieving what we all want."

articles.title: El coche más rápido del mundo sufre un brutal accidente preparando su asalto a los 500 km/h
articles.standfirst: Un YangWang U9 Xtreme se estrelló en China en un test de preparación para el intento de batir su propio récord de velocidad
articles.summary: Un YangWang U9 Xtreme se estrelló en China en un test de preparación para el intento de batir su propio récord de velocidad
articles.body: YangWang, la marca de lujo del gigante chino BYD, asombró al mundo hace apenas poco más de un año al battir el récord absoluto de velocidad de un coche de producción que pertenecía al mítico Bugatti Chiron desde 2019. Lo hizo con su espectacular U9 Xtreme, un deportivo de 3.000 caballos de potencia y propulsión eléctrica, con el que logró un registro de 496,22 km/h. Rozando la cifra mágica de los 500 km/h que, justo desde entonces, se convirtió en el siguiente objetivo del fabricante chino. Y en esa estaba cuando sucedió lo que ahora hemos conocido. El portal ChinaCarNews informa de un terrible accidente en una de las sesiones de prueba del hypercar eléctrico en China en preparación precisamente paraese hito, que podría hacerse oficial dentro de apenas unos días, en la presentación de los planes de expansión internacional de YangWang. Las imágenes del impacto son estremecedoras. El piloto pierde el control del coche a altísima velocidad y el choque contra las protecciones es tan brutal que la carrocería prácticamente se desintegra... aunque el chasis permanece íntegro. De hecho, aunque el piloto fue atendido en la pista por los médicos y después revisado en el hospital, pudo escapar del incidente sin lesiones. Recordemos que el YangWang U9 Xtreme es la versión más salvaje del coupé U9, un superdeportivo eléctrico que está a la venta en China y que, además de por su potencia (la versión estándar tiene 1.305 CV), sorprende por algunas funcionalidades derivadas de su sofisticada suspensión DiSuS-X, que permite controlar los movimientos de la carrocería con tal precisión ... que el coche puede 'bailar' y 'saltar'. Para que el U9 Xtreme pudiera ser acreedor del récord de velocidad de un coche de producción, el fabricante chino entregará una serie limitada a 30 unidades de la variante con cuatro motores eléctricos, de 755 caballos cada uno, para un totoal de 3.000 CV, similar al que logró la plusmarca en Alemania. Además de este mediático récord (que puede ser historia en apenas unos días), el YangWang U9 Xtreme también consiguió la vuelta rápida en el Infierno Verde para un modelo cien por cien eléctrico, con un registro de 6 minutos y 59,157 segundos. Una plusmarca especial ya que se convirtió en el primer eléctrico en bajar de la barrera de los siete minutos en Nürburgring.

articles.title: Carolina Marín: "Quiero poner todo de mi parte para que el bádminton no se olvide en mi país"
articles.standfirst: La campeona olímpica, tricampeona mundial y siete veces campeona de Europa repasa su carrera y habla de sus planes de futuro durante la entrega del MARCA Leyenda
articles.summary: La campeona olímpica, tricampeona mundial y siete veces campeona de Europa repasa su carrera y habla de sus planes de futuro durante la entrega del MARCA Leyenda
articles.body: Cuando Carolina Marín (Huelva, 1993) recibió la noticia de que iba a ser galardonada con el MARCA Leyenda se le puso la carne de gallina. "Mira, mira", nos dijo señalando uno de sus brazos cuando se lo comunicamos. La niña de Huelva que soñaba en grande y con metas que parecían imposibles, es ahora una estrella mundial. PREGUNTA. Su nombre pasa a engrosar la nómina de MARCA Leyendas junto al de Michael Jordan, Pelé, Bolt, Phelps, Nadal, Pau Gasol, Teresa Perales... ¿Qué significa para usted recibir este premio? RESPUESTA. Estoy muy emocionada. Este premio significa mucho. Hay muchos deportistas que se lo merecen. Cuando decimos MARCA y Leyenda se me ponen los pelos de punta. Es muy fuerte. Soy algo consciente de lo que he hecho, pero a veces no lo eres de lo que repercute. Cuando la gente me pregunta qué se siente al ser ejemplo para los niños y las niñas, les contesto que es una bendita responsabilidad. Me siento en paz por lo que he hecho y por reflejar esos valores y que hoy en día se puede abrir un camino. Los sueños se cumplen, pero para cumplirlos uno debe creer en uno mismo y rodearse de una familia ejemplar y un maravilloso equipo. Sin ellos hubiera sido imposible conseguir todo lo que he conseguido. P. Hoy es un referente, pero cuando empezó el suyo era Nadal. ¿Qué era lo que más admiraba de él? R. Yo no tenía referentes en bádminton. Porque en la tele no había. Algo parecido a un referente para mí era Rafa Nadal. Cuando fui a mi primer pabellón, me llamó la atención la raqueta de bádminton acostumbrada a ver las de tenis. Eso, el hecho de que fuera algo diferente, me llamó la atención. Después, he podido ver a Rafa Nadal por la televisión, un deportista que no da nada por perdido. Y después he podido conocerle en persona y para mí es alguien que ha dado siempre ejemplo. P. Acabamos de escuchar a Nadal en un vídeo decirle que la admira, ¿qué siente al oír estas palabras? R. A veces las emociones se sienten tan dentro que es difícil ponerles palabras. Recibí miles de mensajes cuando me rompí la rodilla en París. Yo tenía la necesidad de contestar a todo el que se había tomado su tiempo para escribirme. Me entró un audio de 48 segundos de un número que no tenía guardado. Al final me dice: ‘soy Rafa’. Lo tuve que volver a escuchar. Era un mar de lágrimas. Estoy eternamente agradecida. P. Usted siempre dice que cuando empezó era muy mala jugando, pero le dijo a Fernando Rivas que quería ser la mejor del mundo. A eso se le llama tener confianza en una misma… R. Una niña cuando es pequeña va a Madrid con una mochila cargada de ilusión. Tienes la ilusión de querer ser la mejor en todo en un deporte que en nuestro país era desconocido. Eso es importante para que los niños y niñas veas que todo es posible. Pero hay una condición indispensable que es el esfuerzo. Vivimos en un mundo de inmediatez y hay que recalcar que el esfuerzo encuentra recompensa en un tiempo. Cuando me preguntan por el secreto de nuestros éxitos es sencillo: sólo hay trabajo. Y también renunciar a grandes cosas como a mi hogar y a mi familia para venirme al CAR, de lo que no me arrepiento... Si quieres conseguir algo te tienes que quitar de algunas cosas. Y eso hoy en día es complicado porque parece que se quiere todo. P. 2014 fue el punto de inflexión. Ganó el Europeo y también el Mundial. ¿Qué se Le viene a la cabeza cuando recuerda ese primer oro mundial de los tres que ganó en su carrera? R. Recuerdo muchas cosas. Dos meses antes estuve preparando un partido concreto porque nunca había ganado a una jugadora china, tenía ahí un bloqueo mental. En segunda ronda, me medía a la número 2 y si quería medalla, tenía que ganar. Cuando llegó el día, acabé ganando ese partido 21-9, 21-12. Lo que se dice una paliza. Eso fue porque yo ya había ganado ese partido muchas veces, sabía dónde iba a golpear mi rival. Y eso que hubo encuentros muy complicados. Cuando pasé a semis, recuerdo acabar el partido y decirme Fernando: ‘Tienes medalla. Ahora tienes que ver de qué color’. Dije que el oro, pero cuando me levanté para la final, me dolía todo el cuerpo. Empecé a calentar y me decía que igual tenía que conformarme con la plata. El partido empezó complicado, porque estaba negativa, perdí el primer set e iba abajo también en el segundo, pero Fernando se la jugó, salió y me dijo: ‘Dentro de un rato sonará un himno. De ti depende de si es el de España o el chino. Y pensé, al menos voy a hacer sudar a la china. Pero así fue como poco a poco acabé remontando. Parecía que a las chinas no se les podía ganar, pero se me olvidó el cansancio y acabé ganando. Fue un momento muy feliz. P. En Río 2016 perdió el primer set y tuvo que remontar. Detrás de la medalla dijo que había “dos últimos meses infernales”. ¿Cómo fueron y qué sensaciones tiene al rememorar el día de la final? R. Lo recuerdo todo. Los entrenamientos, algunos con torniquetes. La rueda de prensa previa a empezar a los Juegos. Fui la única deportista española que dijo que iba a ganar el oro. Me fui sin la foto en el Cristo, pero con el oro. Recuerdo todos los días comiendo arroz y pollo. Entrar al pabellón y la gente animando sin parar. Y ese último punto, cuando me tiré al suelo y lloré. Lo que se me vino a la cabeza fueron los entrenamientos previos. Luego llegó el abrazo a Fernando (Rivas) y Anders (Thomsen) y les dije que somos los mejores. Y luego a mi padre y mi madre. Y el abrazo con Alejandro Blanco. P. Se convirtió en un ídolo en Asia, pese a que puso fin a la hegemonía asiática olímpica y mundial... R. Los dos países donde más me admiran son India e Indonesia. En Río, gané a una rival india. Y cuando fui después a la India me recibieron con tambores y mucho cariño y admiración. Jugando torneos allí me animaban casi más a mí que a las jugadoras locales a las que me enfrentaba. P. Después tuvo que reconstruirse con sus tres graves lesiones de rodilla. La segunda de ellas a dos meses de Tokio 2020. ¿De dónde sacaba fuerzas cuando el cuerpo parecía decirle que no podía más? R. Tenía muy claros mis objetivos. Muchos días hubiera pagado por no ir a entrenar. No dormía. Me levantaba y me dolía todo el cuerpo, pero cuando tienes claro qué quieres conseguir, todo merece la pena. P. ¿Echa de menos el bádminton? ¿Ha sentido vacío en algún momento? R. No, no lo echo de menos. Fue una decisión muy complicada tras 24 años, pero ha sido la decisión más sabia que he tomado después de tres lesiones graves. No quería quedarme con la espina clavada de ver qué pasaba, pero uno se da cuenta de que más allá del deporte hay vida y prioricé la salud antes que seguir forzando mi cuerpo. No quería acabar con una prótesis o en silla de ruedas. P. ¿Tiene proyectos relacionados con el bádminton? R. Me daría mucha pena que si Carolina Marín ha colgado su raqueta y ha hecho todo lo que ha hecho en su país por el bádminton, que ahora porque se ha retirado se deje de hablar de bádminton. Espero que haya gente que haga su propio camino y que se siga hablando de bádminton. A día de hoy lo veo complicado, siendo realista y honesta, pero quiero poner todo de mi parte para que no se olvide el bádminton en mi país. Quiero crear una academia, voy a empezar a hacer un clinic de mi deporte a nivel internacional y me encantaría llevarlo también a España. No echo de menos al bádminton como deportista, pero quiero estar involucrada en el bádminton.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on John Cena Classic 'Problems,' Cruz Montana Joining 946 & Nikki Bella vs. Chelsea Green
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE's Reported Original Plans for John Cena Classic

As more information comes to light regarding the John Cena Classic, rumors are also emerging regarding how WWE originally wanted to present the event.

According to Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), the initial idea for the John Cena Classic was a tournament in which the fans voted for who would move on to the next round after each match.

Meltzer noted that such a format would cause issues since WWE would have no way to prepare for subsequent matches ahead of time with the fans making the call on who advances in real time.

During Monday night's episode of Raw, John Cena announced that the John Cena Classic will be held at Disney World in Orlando, Florida, on Dec. 14.

Earlier on the same day, Raw will be held in Australia, meaning there will be two separate episodes of Raw on Dec. 14.

Cena also unveiled the John Cena Classic Championship and revealed that fans will get to vote for the inaugural winner of the championship on Club WWE.

The format of the event remains somewhat unclear, though, as it isn't yet known if it will be a tournament with certain Superstars working multiple times, or if it will merely be a series of matches.

More updates may be relayed Wednesday night when Cena makes a special appearance on NXT.

Another shocking addition was made to the 946 stable on Monday night, as Cruz Montana joined the group.

According to False Finish (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), Royce Keys made the call for Montana to become part of 946.

False Finish previously reported that Keys was the one behind Carmelo Hayes joining 946 as well.

Keys faced Solo Sikoa in the main event of Raw on Monday, but there was not a definitive finish due to interference by 946.

Sikoa escaped further punishment, which allowed for the rest of The Bloodline to make its way down to the ring, leading to a stare-down and a brawl.

Amid the chaos, a masked figure appeared and took out Roman Reigns. The man under the mask revealed himself to be Montana, officially making him the sixth member of 946 along with Keys, Hayes, Jaida Parker, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price.

Montana is scheduled to face Dion Lennox on Wednesday night's episode of NXT, but that figures to be his NXT swan song, as Keys reportedly had his request granted in the form of Montana becoming the latest member of 946.

Now that 946 has five male members and The Bloodline will as well once Jacob Fatu returns, all signs point toward a WarGames match happening at Survivor Series this month.

WWE's Reported Reaction to Green vs. Bella Match

WWE reportedly isn't sweating any fan backlash against the WWE Women's Championship match between Chelsea Green and Nikki Bella from last week's episode of SmackDown.

Although the match was panned by some fans on social media, WWE officials reportedly aren't concerned about the reaction.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), WWE "moved on" and "don't care about" how the Green vs. Bella match is being rated on sites such as Cagematch.net .

WrestleVotes noted that WWE and fans of Bella and Green aren't concerned with their in-ring work as much as they are their merchandise sales, social media impressions and other metrics.

On SmackDown, Green beat Bella to retain the WWE women's title and secure her spot at Crown Jewel this weekend where she will face women's world champion Liv Morgan for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship.

While Green vs. Bella wasn't a technical masterclass by any means, it was effective in terms of solving the conflict between Chelsea and Nikki, and moving the storyline between Green and Morgan forward.

Not every match can or should be a five-star classic, and it sounds as though WWE is well aware of that.

articles.title: Angel Reese faces Sophie Cunningham's blunt criticism after WNBA Finals collapse against Golden State Valkyries
articles.summary: Angel Reese’s strong start to the WNBA Finals could not carry the Atlanta Dream to the title, and Sophie Cunningham believes one part of her game made the
articles.body: Angel Reese’s strong start to the WNBA Finals could not carry the Atlanta Dream to the title, and Sophie Cunningham believes one part of her game made the difference. On the No Hesitation podcast, Cunningham and trainer Drew Hanlen pointed to Reese’s missed layups and her need to finish easy chances. Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds in Game 2, then added 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3. But after Atlanta moved ahead 2-1, Golden State won three of the next four games to claim the championship in seven games overall.Sophie Cunningham and Drew Hanlen Explain Where Angel Reese Needs to ImproveReese looked difficult to stop in the middle of the series. Her 30-point, 16-rebound performance in Game 2 made her the youngest player in WNBA Finals history to reach those numbers in a game. She followed it with another double-double in Game 3, helping Atlanta take control of the series.However, her scoring dropped as the Finals continued. During the latest episode of the No Hesitation podcast, Cunningham and Hanlen discussed why Reese struggled to maintain that form.Cunningham agreed with Hanlen’s view that Reese looked like an MVP when she was finishing her chances near the basket.“She was killing it, and she was literally looking like the MVP because of the consistency of her making her layups,” Cunningham said.She also pointed out that Reese gets plenty of chances close to the basket because of her height and strength. The problem, according to Cunningham, is turning those chances into points regularly.Hanlen added another concern. He said Reese sometimes spends too much time reacting to referees after missing a layup instead of getting back to defend. He also mentioned her technical fouls during the season.Hanlen believes improving her finishing should be a major part of Reese’s work during the offseason.“I know I’m working hard on my three. I know I’m working hard to improve my free throw, but it comes down to layups because I get them. I just got to make them. They’re right there,” Hanlen said.Reese's numbers in the final games explain why the discussion has started. She scored eight points in Game 4 and seven in Game 5, shooting just 4-of-20 combined from the field. She did better in Game 6 with 15 points and 13 rebounds. However, she finished Game 7 with eight points and 12 rebounds as Golden State won 68-63.Dave Portnoy also criticized Reese on the Wake Up Barstool podcast. He questioned her behavior after Game 3 and was particularly harsh about her performances in Atlanta's losses. However, his claim that she did not show up in the final three defeats overlooks her 15-point performance in Game 6.Angel Reese Remains Positive About Atlanta Dream’s Future After Finals LossDespite losing the championship after leading the series 2-1, Reese has not lost faith in her team. She also made it clear that reaching the Finals was something she and her teammates could be proud of.“Just because we didn’t win today doesn’t mean that we won’t be champions in the future,” Reese said.She also thanked her teammates for their support throughout the season.“I’m really proud of the year that I had. I’ve done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn’t be able to do it without this group. I love these girls.”Reese finished the regular season averaging 16.4 points, 12.1 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game. She also led the league in rebounds.The Finals loss will hurt, especially after Atlanta came so close to winning its first championship. But Reese has shown that she can take control of games when her shots are falling. Her next challenge is to become more consistent around the basket and make those chances count when the pressure is highest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mark Walter Reportedly Exploring Partial Sale of Cadillac F1 Stake After Lakers Exit
articles.summary: Billionaire sports franchise owner Mark Walter is consider selling at least part of his stake in Cadillac's Formula 1 team, Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen and The Athletic's Madeline Coleman reported.
articles.body:
Billionaire sports franchise owner Mark Walter is consider selling at least part of his stake in Cadillac's Formula 1 team, Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen and The Athletic's Madeline Coleman reported.

The news comes after Walter agreed to sell the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers and pledged to sell a minority stake in the Premier League team Chelsea.

Walter is also reportedly looking to sell the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks, Bloomberg's Randall Williams, Sridhar Natarajan and Lucas Shaw reported last month.

Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champ

Badenhausen reported Walter has at least seven parties interested in purchasing the Cadillac F1 team "an asking price of at least $3 billion."

Coleman reported Walter is "exploring selling a portion of his stake... but only at a certain price," and added the F1 team's valuation is "above $3 billion."

Cadillac entered F1 as the grid's 11th team this year after General Motors and TWG Global reportedly paid a $450 million expansion fee back in 2024, per the BBC's Andrew Benson.

Walter has control of the F1 team through his holding company TWG Global, which also owns stakes in IndyCar's Andretti Global, IMSA's Wayne Taylor Racing, Supercars' Walkinshaw Andretti United and Formula E's Andretti Global.

Coleman reported TWG Global's motorsports division as of now "is not seeking out buyers for its other properties."

TWG Global stated in August the company was "not considering exiting its stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team or any other part of TWG Motorsports," but also said leadership would "consider all legitimate offers when they are received."

Walter still owns sports properties, including the MLB's Los Angeles Dodgers and the Professional Women's Hockey League.

He recently told the California Post's Jack Harris he plans to retain ownership of the Dodgers "no matter what." The PWHL has previously stated it is not expecting a change in ownership.

Walter is selling the Lakers at a reported valuation of $12.5 billion, per ESPN's Ramona Shelburne . He agreed to sell half of a combined 25 percent stake in Chelsea for a reported payout of around $650 million, per Ben Dummett and Margot Patrick of the Wall Street Journal.

articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. I learned a valuable tip very early in my journalism career: Never read the comments. And for the most part, I follow that rule. But over the weekend, I was out on Old Hickory Lake covering The Champions, a massive bass fishing tournament with a $3.25 million purse. It was also our first big event since OutKick OutDoors became officially official back in August. So naturally, I was curious to see what people were saying. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE And after scrolling the comments, I made an alarming discovery: There are an awful lot of you who think there's some sort of mass bass genocide happening on lakes across the country. Friends, allow me to explain how this works. These tournaments are catch-and-release. Anglers keep their fish alive in aerated livewells on their boats, hold them up for a few quick seconds during weigh-in, and then the fish are returned to the lake. In fact, keeping those fish alive is such a priority that competitors are heavily penalized if they bring a dead fish to the scales. Unfortunately, things do happen sometimes. But the entire process is designed to keep as many of them swimming as possible. And for the record, there's absolutely nothing wrong with legal hunting and fishing, harvesting animals for food. But before y'all come yelling at me for covering bass fishing, please understand we're not out here just murdering smallmouth in droves for funsies. MATT ROBERTSON WINS RECORD $1.25 MILLION FISHING PRIZE, DECLARES 'TRAILER TRASH FOR LIFE' Maybe just relax, grab yourself a beer from the garage fridge, kick back and enjoy some Nightcaps. Megan Moroney and Christian Pulisic are officially official So you can all breathe easier now that we finally have confirmation. After months of dating rumors, suspiciously timed trips to Italy and a phone lock screen that seemingly gave the whole thing away, country music star Megan Moroney and USMNT soccer star Christian Pulisic are officially an item. Apparently, Moroney was chatting with actress Eiza González at the TIME100 Gala in New York City last Thursday when González reportedly joked, "We're the new generation of WAGs." González is dating tennis star Grigor Dimitrov, while Moroney has apparently claimed her spot on Team Pulisic. PEOPLE subsequently confirmed that the country singer and AC Milan star are, in fact, dating. Congratulations to the happy couple. And now we can close this case. Good for the Chicago Bears & Jeffery Simmons Look, it's no secret that I despise the Tennessee Titans. As someone who used to work there, I can confirm the absolute dumpster fire they put out on the field every Sunday is directly reflective of the ownership and front office that runs the place. I was thrilled for Derrick Henry when he got out of Nashville — and for Kevin Byard, too. So now I'm equally pumped that Big Jeff Simmons is in Chicago and will actually have a chance at a ring. And man, did he make one hell of a first impression. As a Miami Dolphins fan, I'll likely never see a Super Bowl in my lifetime. I'm at peace with this. But I'm a Bears fan by marriage, so I hope they keep it up. Check out this free throw form I do not claim to be an expert on the fundamentals of basketball. My hoops career ended in fifth grade when I got frustrated with girls 7 inches taller than me boxing me out in the school gym. But even I know you're not supposed to shoot a free throw like you're trying to launch a grenade over enemy lines. Allow me to introduce you to Kendall Puryear, a 6-foot-3 forward for the University of South Florida women's basketball team, who has perhaps the most unhinged free throw form I've ever seen. Seriously, watch this. WHAT WAS THAT?! Puryear, who transferred from Purdue this offseason, went to the line twice during Monday's 80-54 win over Furman and missed both attempts. Which, given the mechanics we're working with here, isn't exactly shocking. For the record, Puryear was actually a standout shot put thrower in high school, ranking No. 1 in Missouri. Which actually explains a whole lot. But like I said, not a basketball connoisseur over here. We'll need Dan Dakich to weigh in. Let's open the mailbag. 📩 Email: amber.harding@outkick.com (Send your thoughts, stories, tips, rants and photos of your dog.) 🐦 Twitter/X: @TheAmberHarding 📸 Instagram: @amberharding The dog content is here to stay Steve H. writes: Thanks for bringing back dog pictures! We miss the videos too. Tuesday nights used to be my favorite edition of Nightcaps until they disappeared. Duke (yellow lab) took time out of his busy schedule patrolling the yard and scaring away squirrels, rabbits, deer, and sand hill cranes to express his approval too. DF in AR writes: Why so many words on the wnba to an audience that doesn't like the wnba or NBA??? Why not something about the world series? I like your writing but not the subjects woke Fox wants to highlight. I enjoy your personal trips and dog more. How about more words on positive and inspiring topics? Amber: Very kind of you to say, Darrell. Don't worry — the travel/dog content is staying. At least on Tuesdays it is. And on OutKick OutDoors. In Friday's Nightcaps, Zach vowed not to write about the WNBA (except for Sophie Cunningham) for the next seven months. I'm going to make you that same promise. I can't promise I won't throw some Cameron Brink in there occasionally, though. Eric P. (or maybe his dog, Duke) writes: Dogs on vacation?? But of course I need a vacation..just be sure the pool is at the right temperature.. Amber: Always love it when Duke stops by Nightcaps. My Rocky is getting ready for a very busy vacation season. We're leaving today for a little getaway to the woods then next month it's off to Florida for Thanksgiving with the family. And then Indiana for Christmas. OK, Indiana isn't much of a vacation destination, but Rocky's just happy to be included. Very good film and provides you with some additional Brad Pitt eye candy. Best seen in a theater as the cinematography is awesome. Amber: I saw it a couple of weeks ago! Phenomenal film. And I'm woman enough to admit I sobbed. No spoilers here, though. As a German Shepherd haver myself, I know that I'm biased. But man, they are just incredible dogs. Their intelligence, trainability and loyalty are out of this world. But so are their shedding and neediness, so keep that in mind before you go getting one. Life is just better with man’s best friend riding shotgun. articles.title: What happened to Rachel Apa? 24 year old NYC Marathon runner dies near finish line after running for late grandfather's cause
articles.summary: Rachel Apa, a 24-year-old former college field hockey player, died after collapsing just two miles from the finish line of the 2026 New York City Marathon
articles.body: Rachel Apa, a 24-year-old former college field hockey player, died after collapsing just two miles from the finish line of the 2026 New York City Marathon on Sunday, November 1. She was running through Central Park when she suffered a medical emergency around 1:30 p.m. Despite receiving CPR and being rushed to Mount Sinai Medical Center, doctors could not save her life. She was pronounced dead at 9:40 p.m. Her father, Steve Apa, told The New York Times that she died from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition that causes rapid muscle breakdown.Rachel Apa Receives Emergency Help After Collapsing During New York City MarathonRachel was running near Mile 24 in Manhattan's Central Park when she suddenly collapsed. She was just around two miles away from completing her first New York City Marathon.A hospital social worker named Michaela Nicholas was among the first people to reach her. She tried to check Rachel's pulse but could not find one. Two doctors who were watching the race also stepped in and took turns performing CPR, Nicholas told The New York Times.Medical staff from the New York Road Runners (NYRR), the organization behind the marathon, soon arrived with a defibrillator. Paramedics followed and took Rachel to Mount Sinai Medical Center by ambulance.Doctors continued trying to save her for around six hours. However, she died at 9:40 p.m., according to her father.Steve Apa told The New York Times that his daughter died from rhabdomyolysis. It is a serious condition in which muscle tissue breaks down quickly and releases harmful substances into the bloodstream. Intense physical activity can sometimes trigger it.The loss left her family struggling to understand what had happened. Steve described his daughter's condition before the race, saying, "It's unfathomable. Perfect health, perfect shape, 24 years old."The New York Road Runners also shared a statement following her death. The organization said, "We are deeply saddened by the death of one of our runners following yesterday's race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with the runner's family, friends, and the entire running community."Rachel Apa's Final Messages to Her Father and Her Run for Parkinson's FoundationRachel's parents were following her progress throughout the marathon. Her mother, Michelle, was in New York and recorded a video of her daughter smiling at Mile 14 in Queens. Her father, meanwhile, was back home in Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, sending her encouraging messages as she moved through the course.However, Rachel's messages soon began to worry him. At Mile 18, she replied with one word: "Ow." A mile later, she sent another message saying, "Ow ow." Despite the pain, she continued running and later texted her father, "final stretch," at Mile 23. That was the last message he received from her.Michelle was heading towards Central Park to watch her daughter finish when she noticed something unusual on the marathon tracking app. Rachel's location had stopped moving near Mile 24. She rushed towards the location and reached the scene as an ambulance was taking her daughter to the hospital. Michelle then followed in another ambulance.Nicholas, who had rushed to help Rachel, later said she held the young runner's hand after she collapsed so that she would know someone was beside her.Rachel was a graduate of Bucknell University, where she played field hockey. She worked as a product manager for an electrical component company and had also started studying for an MBA at Charleston Southern University.Running the marathon had a special meaning for her. She wanted to raise money for the Parkinson's Foundation in memory of her grandfather, who died from Parkinson's disease in 2022.In her online fundraising message, Rachel explained how much her grandfather had influenced her life."My grandfather was my role model growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement."She also shared how painful it was to watch his illness affect his ability to move. She wrote that she wanted to help raise money and awareness for research, better care, and a cure for Parkinson's disease.Following Rachel's death, NYRR confirmed that she was the first runner to die during the New York City Marathon since 2024.The New York Road Runners said Rachel was the first participant to die following a medical incident during the marathon since 2024. However, CBS New York reported on November 3 that the city's medical examiner's office was investigating her death and had not yet determined an official cause. The information about rhabdomyolysis came from her father.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘A lot of lies’ – Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was ‘right’ to drop him against Bournemouth and denies rift
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes insists there are no issues between him and boss Michael Carrick – and hopes his side’s win over Roma can be the st...
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes insists there are no issues between him and boss Michael Carrick – and hopes his side's win over Roma can be the start of a turnaround this season.

The 3-2 victory provided a much-needed boost for United following a run of nine games without a win.

Fernandes was dropped to the bench for his side's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last month following comments made after their 4-1 loss to Como, in which he questioned the team's approach .

But the United skipper played down any perceived problems between him and Carrick and says he is firmly focused on turning things around.

"The club needed that win, the players needed that win," he told Amazon Prime. "We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together.

"It's been tough, there's been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air after. Nothing like that happened.

"The manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I wasn't performing and that's fair.

"Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept that.

"It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn't change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me."

United have faced mounting pressure following their recent struggles, with supporters growing increasingly frustrated by the team's performances.

Fernandes acknowledged those frustrations but stressed that the players were equally desperate to turn their fortunes around.

"It's been a long time that we didn't get the win and it's been frustrating for them as much as it has been for us too," he said.

"But we didn't take that in the wrong way. We took it in a good way because it's normal, because fans want to win games.

"They've been used to seeing this club at the top winning games and winning trophies and for them it's been so frustrating to see the club in this situation.

"I want to make everyone aware that we are all frustrated with the situation at the moment and we all want to get out of this. Hopefully this win today is the start of something good for us."

Reflecting on the comeback victory over Roma, in which United came from two goals down thanks to a Fernandes penalty and Matheus Cunha double, the Portugal international urged his side to build on the win.

"It's been a tough period for us, we have not been able to perform in the way we want, to get the results we want," he added.

"We've done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a full game to get more results and it's been tough.

"But today was important to get a win. We knew after half-time we still had the fans with us, we felt at any moment that we could change it with a goal and fortunately we did it today."

articles.title: Nebraska vs Illinois Prediction: Bowl Game or Bust?
articles.summary: Both the Huskers and the Illini have five wins, but the loser is in big trouble in the bowl picture. Here's the CFN preview and prediction.
articles.body:
These are testy times for both Illinois and Nebraska. The Illini were supposed to be in for a strong season, but they're scrapping for anything they can get. They might be 5-3, but if they lose this, there's a problem – they'll be the underdog in each of the final three games. Basically, if they want a winning season, they have to beat the Huskers. Meanwhile, Nebraska's season has hit a wall. The 5-0 start was great. The 0-3 run since then, though, has set off an already frustrated fan base desperately waiting for the Huskers to be a powerhouse again. Here's the thing, though: the losses to Indiana, Oregon, and Wisconsin were by a total of 13 points. The Big Red needs more of a tune-up than an overhaul.

Illinois (5-3) won the last meeting 31-24 in 2024, and won four of the last five going back to 2019.

Nebraska (5-3) is in the midst of a nasty run in November, going on the road for three of its last four, with Rutgers next week. Ohio State is the home finale before finishing at Iowa.

The Illini travel to Los Angeles to face UCLA right after this. They come back to host Iowa, and close at Northwestern.

Date: Friday, November 6, 2026 Game Time: 8:00 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Gies Memorial Stadium, Champaign, IL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10

Seriously, all is not lost. This three-game slide is stoppable by doing three key things: stop the turnovers (this actually wasn't a problem until the Washington loss), run better, complete more passes. Essentially, the offense has to be far, far sharper. Scoring more points would be nice, but the offense has to move for that to happen. The Huskers haven't hit 60% of their passes in any of the losses in the three-game losing streak. Illinois allows teams to connect on 66% of their throws. The Illini defense has been hit-or-miss against the run, and it only has six takeaways on the season.

The Illinois defense has found a way to stop teams from scoring points, and Nebraska has a problem putting the biscuit in the basket. Nebraska's attack had a good pace and plenty of movement over the five-game winning streak, and it hasn't scored more than 17 in any of the last three games. But there's a reason for that. Ohio is good, but it's a MAC team. Other than the Bobcats, the other four Nebraska wins came against teams that aren't good at college football, and Indiana, Oregon, and Washington are pretty decent. But for the Illini, it comes down to …

Nebraska vs Illinois Prediction, Betting Lines

Just get one turnover, Illinois. The margin of error for both teams is at a bare minimum, but for the Illini, it's the juice coming off one big takeaway. The team is 5-0 when it generates a turnover, 0-3 when it doesn't. Nebraska will start pushing the attack a little more, which means it'll press, and with it will come at least one important interception.

articles.body:
The Lions announced that linebacker Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury during Sunday's win over the Vikings and they moved him to the injured reserve list.

Rolder was injured on the same play that linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury that has required him to remain hospitalized since Sunday. The fourth-round pick had 11 tackles and a sack in his five appearances during the regular season.

Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that the team will sign linebacker K.J. Britt off of the Patriots' practice squad.

They have another open roster spot at their disposal as well. They announced that defensive back Bishop Fitzgerald has been waived on Tuesday.

Fitzgerald was signed off of the Steelers' practice squad in September, but he never appeared in a game for the Lions.

articles.title: Details emerge following crash that killed 2 Texas Lutheran football players
articles.summary: The service will honor the two student-athletes killed in a Seguin crash, with an online livestream available to the public
articles.body:
Texas Lutheran University is preparing to come together this week to remember two student-athletes killed in a crash in Seguin , as the university's Bulldog community mourns their loss.

The university announced a memorial service for A'Jean (AJ) Augustine, 20, of Houston, and Deyreck Dean, 23, of Rockwall, scheduled for 11 a.m. Thursday, November 5, in Jackson Auditorium.

"The Bulldog Family is devastated by the loss of two of our own this week," the university said in its announcement.

The gathering will give students, faculty, staff, teammates and loved ones an opportunity to celebrate the lives of Augustine and Dean, grieve their absence and pray for their families, according to the university. A short reception will follow the service.

Those unable to attend in person can watch the service through a university livestream.

Augustine and Dean were killed early Monday, November 2, in a single-vehicle crash on State Highway 46 in Seguin, according to police.

The crash was reported at approximately 2:38 a.m. in the 1900 block of State Highway 46 North. A 2012 Kia Sorento was traveling southbound at a high rate of speed when the driver lost control, crossed into the northbound lanes and struck a guardrail, according to a preliminary police report. Both occupants were pronounced dead at the scene.

In an earlier statement to MySA, Texas Lutheran described Augustine and Dean as beloved members of the university community whose loss would be felt across campus.

Both students were connected to the university's football program. Augustine was an active member of the 2026 team, listed as a junior kicker on the Bulldogs' roster. Dean previously played for the team as a senior linebacker, with his athletic eligibility expiring after the 2025 season.

No. 5 Davis (8-3) at No. 4 Herriman (9-2)

All-time series: Herriman leads 2-1 (since 2019)

Last meeting: Herriman won 35-21 at Davis (Oct. 22, 2021, 6A first round)

Davis has been in this round before. A year ago the Darts were the No. 3 seed and lost 41-38 to Lone Peak in the quarterfinals. This time they're the lower seed and on the road, but they're playing better than they were early in the season.

Davis started 3-3. Two of those losses came against the top two seeds in 6A: 51-14 to Corner Canyon and 42-7 at Mountain Ridge. The third was 29-21 to American Fork. The Darts have won five straight since then by a combined 201-75. That run includes an outright Region 1 title and last week's 37-18 first-round win over Farmington. They also beat two 5A quarterfinalists, 56-28 at Fremont and 27-6 at Alta.

The two teams' common opponents can't separate them. Both lost badly to Mountain Ridge, Davis by 35 and Herriman by 38. Both also routed Weber, Davis 52-6 and Herriman 55-6.

Bode Sparrow is the player most likely to swing this game. He scored four touchdowns against Farmington, including a 99-yard kickoff return. He has 62 catches for 882 yards and 18 touchdown catches. He also has four rushing touchdowns and two return touchdowns, and he has 64 tackles on defense. Paden Toula has completed 69.9% of his passes for 1,919 yards and 22 touchdowns. Jaxton Itaaheau has 11 total touchdowns, and Sam Coleman has 50 catches. Coleman also leads the defense with four interceptions and has a defensive touchdown and a return touchdown.

To win, Davis has to slow down Filisi Filipe, and that has to start with Ben Dorius (10 sacks) and the front seven. Dexter Frasure leads the team with 83 tackles. Davis's own running game averages 4.5 yards per carry, so Toula and Sparrow will have to carry the offense. Herriman's defense has 15 interceptions, so Toula can't afford mistakes. Davis has won three region titles in four seasons under Scott Peery. The program's last state title came in 2004.

Herriman's plan is to give the ball to Filipe. He has run for 1,542 yards and 27 touchdowns at 9.2 yards per carry, and with three touchdown catches he has 30 total touchdowns. He ran for 134 yards and four touchdowns against Weber last week. Max Stevens adds 557 yards at 7.3 yards per carry. As a team, the Mustangs average 7.6 yards per carry and have 36 rushing touchdowns.

Herriman can beat teams in more than one way. Bryson Sweeney has thrown for 1,860 yards and 19 touchdowns with five interceptions, and Hayes Priest leads the team with 46 catches. The Mustangs average 38.3 points per game, third in 6A. They allow 16.3, also third. Their wins include 25-14 over Bountiful, the 5A No. 4 seed and a 5A quarterfinalist, 40-36 at Stansbury, the 4A No. 3 seed, 48-7 at Westlake and 44-0 over Bingham. Their only losses were 22-20 at home to Lehi and 45-7 at unbeaten Mountain Ridge.

The defense creates turnovers and big plays. Kemper Castro has 11 sacks, and Ashton Hebert and Aden Jensen have six each, for 28 as a team. Hebert also returned a fumble 39 yards for a touchdown against Weber. Logan Gregory and Aden Perea have four interceptions each. Perea has two defensive touchdowns and Gregory has a return touchdown. Brody Crayk has made four field goals.

The concern is close games. Herriman lost to Lehi by two and beat Copper Hills only 23-20, and Davis has the kind of playmakers who can turn a game in a few plays. Herriman also needs to keep Sparrow from breaking a big kick return. The Mustangs lost 22-14 to Mountain Ridge in last year's quarterfinals, and Matt Rickards' team is trying to get past this round. The winner plays the Skyridge–American Fork winner. American Fork beat Davis 29-21 in September.

Nate Childs had six days to get ready. Starter Jake Matsen broke his collarbone early in the Oct. 8 loss to Corner Canyon, and American Fork's season went to a senior who had started much of last year and had waited behind Matsen this fall. Childs' first start came on the road at Skyridge, against the No. 1 seed and the team that ended the Cavemen's season a year ago.

The game started badly. Beckham Bennett scored on two short runs in the first quarter, and Skyridge led 14-0. Then American Fork settled in. The Cavemen outscored the Falcons 15-7 the rest of the way. With 8:21 left, Childs threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Zack Cowie and ran in the two-point conversion himself to make it 21-15. That was as close as they got.

Last week Childs looked more comfortable. He threw two touchdown passes in a 32-21 first-round win over Copper Hills, and DC Fonua returned an interception 34 yards for a touchdown and later ran for another. Childs now gets a second chance at Skyridge, with three more weeks of first-team snaps than he had in the first meeting. If American Fork avoids another slow start, this rematch could look different.

American Fork has beaten good teams this season. It won 29-21 at Davis, the 6A No. 5 seed, and 28-24 at Lone Peak, the No. 7 seed. It also won road games at 5A quarterfinalist Pleasant Grove (36-16) and at Timpview (28-26). The Cavemen's October slide began with a 20-19 home loss to Lehi on Oct. 2. Matsen got hurt the next week, and the losses to Corner Canyon and Skyridge followed.

The defense is American Fork's best chance. Noah Behm has six interceptions and two defensive touchdowns, and he's also the second-leading receiver, with four touchdown catches. Dalin Afu has four sacks and two defensive touchdowns, and Sam Thompson has four sacks. Skyridge quarterback Jagger Fountaine has thrown 11 interceptions, so turnovers are American Fork's clearest path to an upset. Cash Taiese (57 catches, 743 yards, 7 TDs) is Childs' top target, and Jace Worthington has made nine field goals.

There's a lot of history on the line. Skyridge has won five straight in this rivalry, including a 56-29 win in last year's quarterfinals. Aaron Behm, in his 17th season, has taken American Fork to three state title games. This year he'll need to win at Skyridge to get to the semifinals.

Skyridge has won close games all season. Six of its eight regular-season wins came by eight points or fewer, including a 27-24 win at Lone Peak, a 28-20 win at Lehi and the 21-15 win over American Fork. The Falcons have won nine straight since losing 41-26 at Mountain Ridge in the opener. They won Region 3 outright at 4-0, and their 37-27 win over defending champion Corner Canyon is one of the best wins in 6A this season. Last week they beat Riverton 45-0, their first shutout of the year.

The common opponents favor Skyridge. It beat Lehi, a team that beat American Fork. It beat Corner Canyon by 10, and American Fork lost to the Chargers by 24. Both teams won at Lone Peak by three or four points.

Fountaine leads an offense that spreads the ball around. He has thrown for 2,559 yards and 22 touchdowns and run for four more. Four receivers have at least 314 yards. Omarian Sanders leads them with 45 catches, 662 yards and seven touchdowns, and he caught two touchdown passes against Riverton. Bennett has 13 total touchdowns: 10 rushing and three receiving. He also has 41 catches, and he scored both of Skyridge's first-quarter touchdowns in the first meeting. Evan Kopp has made five field goals.

The defense makes big plays. Ethan Schriever has five interceptions and a defensive touchdown. Sa Tanuvasa has 78 tackles and three interceptions, and Rex Caswell has 77 tackles. Sua Ripley leads the team with seven sacks, and Jackson Horsley has also scored on defense.

Skyridge's main concern is the second half. American Fork outscored the Falcons over the final three quarters last time, and Fountaine's 11 interceptions give the Cavemen chances. Skyridge has also seen Childs only once as a starter, and he has played better since. Justin Hemm took Skyridge to the 6A title game in his first season and to the semifinals last year, where it lost 13-7 to Lone Peak. The winner plays the Herriman–Davis winner. Lone Peak has made this kind of run before. A year ago the Knights were the No. 6 seed. They won 41-38 at No. 3 seed Davis in the quarterfinals and beat No. 2 seed Skyridge 13-7 in the semifinals, then lost the championship game to Corner Canyon. To get back to the semifinals, they'll need another upset, this time on the road against the only unbeaten team in 6A.

Lone Peak's record doesn't show how good its defense is. Two of its five losses came against national powers: 59-3 to IMG Academy (Fla.) and 38-14 to Bishop Gorman (Nev.). In its other nine games, Lone Peak allowed 16.1 points per game. Its losses to American Fork (28-24) and Skyridge (27-24) were decided by a combined seven points. Lone Peak won its first-round game the way it wins most games, with defense and special teams. Zachary Zolman made field goals of 48 and 38 yards. To pull the upset, Lone Peak has to keep the score low, and Westlake showed it can be done. Lone Peak needs long drives with Ayden Laws (545 yards) and Pili Mounga (362 yards), and it needs to settle for field goals rather than come away empty. Ball security is the risk. Lone Peak's quarterbacks have thrown 14 interceptions, and its offense can't afford to give Mountain Ridge short fields.

Mountain Ridge's job is to protect the ball and keep Lone Peak's special teams from changing the game. The Sentinels lead 6A in scoring offense (45.9 ppg) and scoring defense (11.0 ppg). They beat every 6A team on their schedule, including No. 1 seed Skyridge (41-26), No. 4 seed Herriman (45-7), No. 5 seed Davis (42-7) and No. 6 seed Westlake (21-13). Syracuse has been here before, in almost exactly the same way. A year ago the Titans beat Westlake 31-28 in the second round and then went to Corner Canyon for the quarterfinals. Ledger Wight's 40-yard touchdown pass and 8-yard run cut the lead to 28-14 before halftime, but the Chargers shut them out in the second half and won 56-14.

This fall the Titans took the same route back. Last Friday they won 35-19 at Westlake. Parker Moffat caught a 55-yard touchdown pass and returned a kickoff 98 yards for another score. Wight threw a touchdown pass and ran 28 yards for one. Now Syracuse returns to Corner Canyon, and this time Wight is a more experienced quarterback.

Wight has completed 59.9% of his passes for 1,969 yards and 22 touchdowns, with only six interceptions, and he has run for 619 yards at 7.2 yards per carry. Kao Prom has 15 total touchdowns: 11 rushing, three receiving and one on defense. Moffat (750 yards) and Bo Metcalfe (519 yards) have seven touchdown catches each. Metcalfe has also scored on defense. Jed Beutler has made five field goals. Syracuse averages 32.6 points per game, fifth in 6A.

The Titans' record undersells them. Two of their four losses came by a combined four points, 27-26 at Woods Cross and 36-33 to Bountiful, and both of those teams are still alive in the 5A quarterfinals. Syracuse also beat 5A quarterfinalist Alta 28-7 and shut out Layton 30-0. Its only loss to a 6A team was 49-35 to Davis. Corner Canyon beat Davis 51-14, which shows the gap Syracuse has to close.

To pull the upset, Syracuse needs pressure and takeaways. Jaxon Pehrson has thrown 11 interceptions, and Jace Cook (6 sacks) and Tay Burgoyne (4 sacks) need to make him uncomfortable. The Titans also have to keep a fast start from turning into another 21-0 deficit. In his third season, Mitch Tulane has a chance to do something last year's team couldn't.

Eric Kjar built Corner Canyon into a dynasty, and the last three titles of his run came in 2023, 2024 and 2025. When Kjar left for Weber State, the job went to Casey Sutera, who had been his defensive coordinator when the Chargers won three straight titles from 2018 to 2020. Now, in his first season as Corner Canyon's head coach, Sutera is trying to give the program something it has never had: a fourth straight state title.

The Chargers started that run with a 35-7 win over Bingham. They scored four first-half touchdowns, including touchdown passes from Pehrson to Beckham Coon and Kelen Gold, and Braxton Sneddon scored one touchdown rushing and another receiving.

Corner Canyon averages 40.5 points per game and allows 13.5, both second in 6A behind Mountain Ridge. Its only losses were 38-24 at Liberty (Ariz.) and 37-27 at No. 1 seed Skyridge. It went 6-1 against 6A playoff teams, beating Davis 51-14, Lone Peak 37-14, American Fork 41-17, Lehi 34-7 and Bingham twice. It has won four straight since the Skyridge loss.

Big plays drive the offense. Pehrson averages 18.5 yards per completion and has 32 total touchdowns, 26 passing and six rushing. Coon averages 29.4 yards per catch and Gold averages 24.8, and each has seven touchdown catches. Diesel Dart has 11 total touchdowns: eight receiving, two rushing and one on defense. Jackson Carruth has run for 1,043 yards and eight touchdowns. Carson Burnett has made six field goals and leads the team with 75 points.

The defense is what makes Corner Canyon hard to beat. Wyatt Warner has 14 sacks and Jack West has six, part of a 35-sack unit. Will Tenney has scored three defensive touchdowns, and Josh Harris has two interceptions and two return touchdowns. Tate Patterson leads the team with 90 tackles. The Chargers have seven defensive touchdowns this season.

The concern is Pehrson's interceptions. Wight has protected the ball well all season, and Syracuse has scored at least 23 points in all but one game. Even so, Corner Canyon has won all three meetings since 2019, and its defense hasn't allowed more than 17 points since the Skyridge game. The Chargers are two wins from the title game. The winner plays the Mountain Ridge–Lone Peak winner. Corner Canyon beat Lone Peak 37-14 in September.

articles.title: Injury update on Terrence Hill Jr., returns for Tennessee basketball vs. Wofford
articles.summary: Junior point guard Terrence Hill Jr. recovered from an ankle injury in time to play in Tennessee basketball's season opener vs. Wofford.
articles.body:
Tennessee basketball will have its starting point guard available for the 2026-27 season opener .

Junior point guard Terrence Hill Jr., who suffered an ankle injury in the No. 9 Vols' exhibition game at Duke, entered at the 17:06 mark of the first half vs. Wofford at Food City Center on Nov. 3 (6 p.m., SEC Network).

Junior guard Juke Harris, who missed the Vols' secret scrimmage vs. Davidson, entered at the same time. He was expected to return to action for the season opener, UT coach Rick Barnes said on Oct. 29.

Hill turned early in the first half of the Vols' 103-64 loss at Duke on Oct. 20. Barnes said after the game that Hill turned his ankle when it was inadvertently stepped on.

Tennessee basketball, Rick Barnes at Duke, exhibition game, top photos

He needed more time to recover, but had been doing individual work and returned to practice on Oct. 29. Barnes wasn't sure of Hill's status for the season opener when he spoke to the media that same day.

A transfer from VCU, Hill scored 22 points on 9-for-17 shooting in the loss to Xavier on Oct. 15 at Food City Center. He knocked down a pair of free throws before suffering the injury against Duke.

Stephen Thompson covers Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball. Email him at stephen.thompson@knoxnews.com and follow him on X @stephenethom.

articles.title: How rested UTSA aims to stay sharp at Florida Atlantic
articles.summary: The Roadrunners' open week came at the "perfect time," Jeff Traylor said, but UTSA is still wary of any complacency during a five-game winning streak.
articles.body:
With a little extra time to recover as UTSA enjoyed an 11-day break between games, safety Elijah Newell said he savored some quiet moments at home, cooking up steaks and watching football as a fan.

The Roadrunners entered the open date 7-1 overall and 4-0 in the American Conference, and Traylor said he was on alert to ensure a sense of complacency didn't start to creep in. Even in restful moments, Newell said he remains driven by memories of UTSA's struggles during 7-6 seasons the past two years.

The Roadrunners returned to work after their brief break with the same steady practice habits they've shown all season, Traylor said, but the real test of how UTSA handled the open week will arrive in a matchup against Florida Atlantic at 6:30 p.m. Thursday in Boca Raton, Fla.

"I hope we're desperate and not prosperous," Traylor said. "I hope we don't sit around and read all of our press clippings, and believe we're really that good."

The Roadrunners wouldn't have to look very hard to find fuel for their egos. The 7-1 start is UTSA's best since 2023, and the team is receiving top-25 votes in both the coaches and Associated Press polls.

The team's five-game winning streak is the longest since 2023, and UTSA stands as one of just two teams with unbeaten records in American competition, joining North Texas.

But quarterback Owen McCown, who said he took advantage of some extra time during the open week to visit family, said the team returned as ready as ever to get back to work.

"Just can't buy into the outside noise," McCown said. "I know there's a lot of talk right now, and our record's really good, but you have to look at it like you're 0-0."

Traylor said he keeps the Roadrunners sharp by emphasizing that any of their four one-score wins could've ended differently, or by harping on mistakes like three lost turnovers and three pre-snap penalties in UTSA's most recent 42-19 win at Tulane.

Still, he's aimed to take some of the physical pressure off the players through this period, holding practices without pads while focusing on fundamentals and technique. Though the Roadrunners have avoided many major injuries this year, Traylor said much of the roster is "limping home."

"We needed it just for our own mental and physical well-being right now," Traylor said. "If you can make it through your first eight games, which we did, and get a bye right now, it's about the perfect time to get one."

The Roadrunners are also heading into the time of the year that has typically been their best, as UTSA is 18-5 in November during Traylor's tenure.

McCown said the biggest key is newcomers and first-time starters developing a feel for the team, and the results have already started to show. After Traylor said the Roadrunners "weren't very good" and "just survived" early in the season, UTSA posted its largest margin of victory this year in the win against Tulane.

"When you're just incrementally getting better a little bit each day, it'll stack up over time, and you're playing your best ball at the time of the year that's the most important time of year to play great ball," Traylor said.

But turning to the later stages of the calendar also brings the potential for new distractions. Traylor has already faced plenty of speculation about his candidacy for the open job at Baylor after Dave Aranda was fired on Oct. 25, addressing the situation with the players.

Each week will likely bring new job openings, and many of those could spark a fresh batch of rumors about Traylor's future with UTSA.

"He tells us it's just a credit of the work we put out there. I think that's normal," McCown said. "Any winning program, especially at our level, he'll start to get those rumors. So, we don't care about it too much. We're just worried about the season."

articles.title: Lake Mary breaks through First Coast blockade in Region 1-3A golf
articles.summary: The stage was set for a First Coast domination of the boys Region 1-3A golf tournament. However, Lake Mary crashed the party and beat Ponte Vedra by one.
articles.body:
Lake Mary crashed the First Coast party in Port Orange.

Led by co-medalist Riley Sillaway with a 3-under 69, the Rams won the FHSAA boys Region 1-3A golf tournament on Nov. 2 at the Golf Club at Cypress Head, nosing out Ponte Vedra by one shot at 6-over-par 294.

Tocoi Creek and Spruce Creek tied for third, another four shots back. Beachside was fifth, six shots off the lead and Creekside sixth, nine shots back.

Ponte Vedra entered the tournament first among Class 3A teams in the state on the iWanamaker rankings, while Lake Mary was fourth and Tocoi Creek fifth. Beachside was seventh and finished second to the Toros in the District 3-3A tournament last week.

The stage was set for a First Coast domination but the Rams, who have won five state championships in the highest division since 2004, had other idea.s

The one-stroke difference between the Rams and Sharks could be found in the early holes at Cypress Head. The four players whose score counted for Lake Mary played the first four holes at 1-under and Ponte Vedra's four played them at 4-over.

James Nagle, Maxwell Morgan and Jake Mason tied as low Sharks players at 1-over 73.

Carson Perry of Spruce Creek tied Sillaway for medalist. Ambrose Kinnare of Tocoi Creek, Charlie Hipp of Creekside and Vishruth Badiga of Lake Mary tied for third at 1-under 71.

Based on the iWanamaker rankings, Beachside and Creekside should reach the Class 3A state tournament Nov. 13-14 at the Mission Inn Resort in Howey-in-the-Hills as at-large teams, with Nease another possibility. The state tournament field will be finalized next week.

Lily Wachter eagle-two caps big day for Beachside

Freshman Lily Wachter drove the green of the par-4 17th hole and drained a 17-foot putt for eagle to play five holes at 4-under and finish with a 67 at the Hawkstone Country Club in Gainesville to lead the Barracudas to the Region 1-3A team title by two shots over Ponte Vedra.

Wachter, who started her round with birdies at Nos. 1, 2 and 4, rallied from a double bogey at the par-5 ninth hole and defeated Nina Santiago of the Sharks by three shots. She drove the 17th green from 236 yards out to set up her eagle putt.

Olivia Connell of Beachside tied for fourth with a 72 and Aspen Bikowski of Bartram Trail finished sixth with a 73.

Boys regional roundup: Bolles outlasts Providence

All five Bolles players shot 77 or lower and the Bulldogs won the Region 1-1A tournament at the King & Bear by nine shots over Providence. Nico Vasto led the Bulldogs with a 74 and Brendan Walrath added a 75. Ethan Grossman led Providence with a 73, tying Brody Mitchell of Maclay for second individually. Hunter Glantz of Florida High was the medalist with a 70. … Live Oak Suwannee's Ty Hurst was the Region 1-2A medalist with a 67 at the Fort Walton Beach Country Club on Nov. 2 and the Bulldogs finished second by 13 shots to Gulf Breeze. Michael Rattigan of Wolfson (75) tied for fifth to lock down an individual spot in the state tournament. Colson Hale of Fernandina Beach (76) tied for seventh.

Girls regional roundup: Sophia Moody on fire

Fleming Island sophomore Sophia Moody shot 4-under 32 on the front nine at the Quail Heights Country Club in Lake City and went on to win the Region 1-2A individual title with a 6-under 65 on Nov. 3. She defeated Lily Martin of South Walton Beach Santa Rosa by one shot and Lily Chiang of Stanton by three. Santa Rosa (305) won the team title by 24 shots over Stanton. … Moody is a combined 11-under in the first two rounds of the postseason and she has shot 69, 66, 67 and 66 in her last four 18-hole rounds. … The Bolles girls got three players in the 70s and won the Region 1-1A tournament on Nov. 2 at Eagle Harbor by 21 shots over Providence. Chloe McGrath led the Bulldogs to their 11th tournament victory of the season with a 73. Sahana Chokshi of Episcopal birdied her first three holes and went on to win the individual title with a 4-under 68 to assure her a spot in the Class 1A state tournament Nov. 17-18. It's the second year in a row she has won or tied as region medalist. Providence was led by Honor Donaldson, who finished second to Chokshi with a 71 that included an eagle at the par-5 12th hole. … Weather has delayed the Region 2-1A tournament at the Cocoa Beach Country Club to Nov. 6. Aubrey Brooks of Keystone Heights is playing as an individual.

articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers 2026 Schedule, Week-By-Week Analysis
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will have a new look in 2026, with a new head coach and more as change unfolds […]
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will have a new look in 2026, with a new head coach and more as change unfolds around the historic organization.

With the Steelers winning the AFC North in 2025, they'll also be facing a first-place schedule for the first time since 2021.

PITTSBURGH STEELERS 2026 SCHEDULE ANALYSIS

WEEK 10: Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday, Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m., NBC

The Steelers head to Cincinnati with painful memories from their last trip to Paycor Stadium, where Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins fueled an offensive explosion in prime time. One possible silver lining for Pittsburgh: this matchup won't feature a Mike Tomlin–led team on Thursday Night Football, a setting that has historically been unforgiving.

It will, however, feature Tomlin, as the former Steelers coach will be in the building for NBC's Football Night in America pregame show, his debut broadcast with his former team.

WEEK 11: Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles, Sunday, Nov. 22, 4:25 p.m., CBS

The Keystone Clash returns to Philadelphia, where history is firmly against Pittsburgh. Jalen Hurts has never lost to the Steelers, and Pittsburgh has not won in Philadelphia since 1965. A road win here would be well outside the norm and one of the more surprising results on the schedule.

WEEK 12: Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh Steelers, Friday, Nov. 27, 3 p.m., Amazon Prime

The Pittsburgh Steelers will host the Denver Broncos on Black Friday, the first time the Steelers have ever played on the day after Thanksgiving. The game will be streamed via Amazon Prime , and will also be available over-the-air in the Pittsburgh market, on a station to be named at a later date.

It will mark just the sixth time the Steelers have played on a Friday, and the first time since 1946. The Steelers were 3-2 in five all-time Friday games, with their last game a 14-7 home win over the Chicago Cardinals at Forbes Field to open the 1946 season on Sept. 20.

The NFL has traditionally set aside Friday nights for high school football and that was codified into law via the Sports Broadcasting Act of 1961, which prohibits the NFL from broadcasting games after 6 p.m. on Friday nights or Saturdays between the second Friday in September and the second Saturday in December,.

That's why the Black Friday game must kick off at 3 p.m., but with the day after Thanksgiving a day off for many Americans, the NFL and Amazon Prime Video decided to pursue playing a game during the day.

The first Black Friday game was in 2023, when the Miami Dolphins beat the New York Jets . The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 and the Chicago Bears beat the Philadelphia Eagles last season.

The Steelers last faced the Broncos in 2024, when they went on the road for a 13-7 win Denver. The last game between the teams at Acrisure Stadium was a 27-19 Steelers win in 2021. Pittsburgh has won the last three games between the teams overall.

WEEK 13: Houston Texans at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Dec. 6, 8:20 p.m, NBC

This matchup carries a bitter edge. The Houston Texans eliminated the Steelers in the Wild Card round less than a season ago, winning 30–6 in what ultimately became Mike Tomlin's final game as head coach. With that loss still fresh, it's hard to imagine this game won't feel personal for Pittsburgh.

The game will also feature Tomlin on the NBC Football Night in America broadcast crew live in Pittsburgh.

WEEK 14: Pittsburgh Steelers at Jacksonville Jaguars, Monday, Dec. 15, 8:15 p.m., ESPN

The Steelers travel to Jacksonville to face Trevor Lawrence , who is 1–0 against Pittsburgh after a rain-soaked win at Acrisure Stadium in 2022. Prior to that, the Steelers had won their previous two games in Duval, including a historic comeback led by Ben Roethlisberger in 2018. New coach Liam Coen will be eager to rewrite Jacksonville's uneven home history against Pittsburgh.

WEEK 15: Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Dec. 20, 1 p.m., CBS

The Steelers will host the Baltimore Ravens in what is almost always one of the NFL's most physical matchups. The last time these two met in Pittsburgh, the game carried massive implications, a winner-take-all showdown for the AFC North. Pittsburgh emerged victorious after a heartbreaking missed field goal by Ravens kicker Tyler Loop , a moment that still stings in Baltimore and fuels the rivalry even further.

WEEK 16: Carolina Panthers at Pittsburgh Steelers, Date/Time TBD

History is firmly stacked against the Carolina Panthers. Carolina has never defeated the Steelers in Pittsburgh and hasn't beaten Pittsburgh anywhere since 1996, the only win in franchise history against them. Still, after a season in which the Panthers nearly upset Matthew Stafford 's Rams in the playoffs, a revamped Carolina team led by Bryce Young could arrive eager to finally make history.

This game will be played on either Saturday, Dec. 26 or Sunday, Dec. 27.

WEEK 17: Pittsburgh Steelers at Tennessee Titans, Sunday, Jan. 3., 1 p.m., CBS

Pittsburgh enters Nashville looking to continue its recent success against the Tennessee Titans. The Steelers' last trip to Nissan Stadium resulted in a 27–24 win in 2020, when former Steelers offensive coordinator Arthur Smith was calling plays for Tennessee. Since then, the teams have met twice in Pittsburgh, both Steelers victories.

WEEK 18: Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens, Date/Time TBD

Pittsburgh travels to M&T Bank Stadium aiming for its second straight road win against the Baltimore Ravens. Last season's matchup ended in a Steelers victory , but not without controversy, as a late Isaiah Likely touchdown was ruled incomplete. This game also marks a turning point in the rivalry, as it will be one of the first times in nearly two decades that John Harbaugh and Mike Tomlin are not both leading their respective sidelines.

This game will be played on either Saturday, Jan. 9, or Sunday, Jan. 10.

WEEK 1: Atlanta Falcons at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Sept. 13, 1 p.m., FOX

For just the second time in 12 seasons, the Steelers will open up the 2026 season on their home turf. The Steelers will host the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium to kick off the 2026 season at 1 p.m. on Sunday, Sept. 13.

The Steelers went eight years without opening the regular season at home from 2015-22, a process that includes random chance, but also reflects the realities of two teams sharing parking facilities on the North Shore.

The Steelers and Pittsburgh Pirates cannot play at the same time, and rarely play on the same day, because they both sell parking in the same lots. This season, the Pirates are on the road for a six-day trip to Chicago, where they will play the White Sox and the Cubs, during the opening week of the NFL season.

Things didn't go so well for the Steelers the last time they opened at home. They were demolished, 30-7, by the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10, 2023. They beat the Cleveland Browns , 30-27, in 2014 for their last Week 1 home win. The Steelers and Falcons will be meeting in the first week of the season for the second time in three years. The clubs met in Atlanta for Week 1 in 2024, with the Steelers winning 18-10 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, with Justin Fields helping guide the offense on the road and Chris Boswell providing all the scoring with six field goals.

The Steelers have won five straight against the Falcons overall, and have not lost to Atlanta in Pittsburgh ever, with a perfect 7-0-1 record against the Falcons in Pittsburgh. The Falcons' last trip to Pittsburgh came in 2018, a convincing 41–17 Steelers win highlighted by Antonio Brown surpassing 100 receiving yards.

WEEK 2: Pittsburgh Steelers at New England Patriots , Sunday, Sept. 20, 1 p.m., CBS

The Steelers return to Foxborough, Mass. hoping to build on last season's 21–14 win over the Patriots at Gillette Stadium. That game came before Drake Maye and a revamped New England roster found their footing. The Patriots also turned the ball over five times, a flaw Mike Vrabel will almost certainly have corrected.

The Patriots will have some extra rest, as they are playing in the season opener in a Super Bowl LX rematch against the Seattle Seahawks . This game will serve as New England's home opener.

WEEK 3: Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Sept. 27, 1 p.m., CBS

The Cincinnati Bengals come to Pittsburgh after the teams split their season series last year. While the Steelers dominated the Bengals at Acrisure Stadium, that win came without star quarterback Joe Burrow under center. With Burrow expected to be healthy, Cincinnati will arrive motivated, and likely looking for revenge.

WEEK 4: Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns, Thursday, Oct. 1, 8:15 p.m., Amazon Prime

Trips to the Dawg Pound have quietly become troublesome for Pittsburgh. The Steelers have not won in Cleveland since Ben Roethlisberger was under center. Last season's loss was especially costly, as Pittsburgh failed to beat a four-win Browns team with the AFC North on the line, making this venue a lingering mental hurdle.

Thursday Night Football has been unkind to the Steelers, as well. Pittsburgh is 0-9 against AFC North opponents on TNF on the road and 14-22 all-time.

WEEK 5: Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Oct. 11, 1 p.m., CBS

The Indianapolis Colts historically struggle in Pittsburgh, and that trend continued last season when the Steelers defeated Indianapolis in a chaotic game where the Colts turned the ball over seven times . If Indianapolis hopes to change its narrative at Acrisure Stadium, protecting the football will be non-negotiable.

WEEK 6: Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers , Sunday, Oct. 18, 1 p.m., CBS

Pittsburgh's matchup with Tampa Bay brings a familiar name in Baker Mayfield . While Mayfield is 2–5 against the Steelers, his most memorable win came in Cleveland's Wild Card upset in Pittsburgh. The Buccaneers, however, typically struggle against the Steelers. The most recent meeting came in 2022, when Mitch Trubisky out-dueled Tom Brady during Brady's farewell season.

WEEK 7: Pittsburgh Steelers vs. New Orleans Saints , at Stade de France, Paris, France, Sunday, Oct. 25, 9 a.m., NFL Network

For the second year in a row, the Steelers will be treading new ground, as they will be a part of the first-ever NFL game in France, one year after playing the first regular season game in Ireland.

The 2026 NFL Paris Game will be held at the Stade de France, which was built in 1998 and at over 81,000 seats, is France's largest stadium. The Stade de France is primarily the home venue for the French national football team and the French national rugby union team.

The Steelers have also played an international game in London, facing the Vikings at Wembley Stadium in 2013.

WEEK 8: Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers, Sunday, Nov. 1, 1 p.m., CBS

Turnabout is fair play. Last year, the Steelers caught the jet-lagged Cleveland Browns after they returned from a trip to London. This year, it'll be the Browns who are benefitting from the Steelers being tired after they return from Paris.

The Browns bring an infamous statistic with them to Pittsburgh. Cleveland has not won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, a drought that spans more than two decades. While the Browns did stun the Steelers in the 2021 postseason, the regular-season curse remains intact. Cleveland will be desperate to finally flip the script in one of the league's most hostile environments.

Alan Saunders and Brendan Howe contributed.
